title.zh: 卷一百四十八 列傳第三十五: 董俊 嚴實
title.en: Volume 148 Biographies 35: Dong Jun, Yan Shi
title.raw: 卷一百四十八 列傳第三十五: 董俊 嚴實 Volume 148 Biographies 35: Dong Jun, Yan Shi

sentences.zh: 董俊子文蔚 文用 文忠 文直

translations.literal: Dong Jun — his sons Wenyue, Wenyong, Wenzhong, and Wenzhi
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jun, with his sons Wenyue, Wenyong, Wenzhong, and Wenzhi

sentences.zh: 董俊字用章，真定藁城人。

translations.literal: Dong Jun, courtesy name Yongzhang, was a native of Gaocheng in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jun, styled Yongzhang, came from Gaocheng in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 少力田，長涉書史，善騎射。

translations.literal: In youth he worked the fields with his strength; as he grew he studied books and history, and was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he labored in the fields; in maturity he delved into books and history, and became adept at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 金貞祐間，邊事方急，藁城令立的募兵，射上中者拔為將。

translations.literal: During the Jin Jinyou era, frontier affairs were urgently pressing. The magistrate of Gaocheng set up a target to recruit soldiers; whoever hit the target would be promoted to commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jin Jinyou period, when the border crisis was acute, Gaocheng's magistrate posted a target to raise troops — anyone who scored a hit would be made a commander.

sentences.zh: 衆莫能弓，獨俊一發破的，遂將所募兵迎敵。

translations.literal: None of the crowd could draw the bow; Jun alone, with one shot, struck the target. He then led the recruited troops to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: No one else could even draw the bow. Jun alone hit the mark with a single shot and went on to lead the newly raised troops against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 歲乙亥，國王木華黎帥兵南下，俊遂降。

translations.literal: In the year yihai, the prince Muqali led troops south; Jun thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the yihai year, Prince Muqali marched south at the head of his army, and Jun submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以勞擢知中山府事，佩金虎符。

translations.literal: In jimao, for his merit he was promoted to administer the affairs of Zhongshan Prefecture, and wore the golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In jimao, rewarded for his service, he was appointed to administer Zhongshan Prefecture and granted the golden tiger tally of command.

sentences.zh: 金將武僊據真定，定武諸城皆應僊。

translations.literal: The Jin general Wu Xian held Zhending, and the cities of Ding and Wu all responded to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general Wu Xian occupied Zhending, and the prefectures of Ding and Wu all rallied to his side.

sentences.zh: 俊率衆夜入真定，逐僊走之，定武諸城復去僊來附。

translations.literal: Jun led his forces by night into Zhending, drove Xian off in flight, and the cities of Ding and Wu again left Xian and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Jun led his men in a night assault on Zhending, putting Wu Xian to flight; the cities of Ding and Wu thereupon abandoned him and rejoined Jun.

sentences.zh: 庚辰春，金大發兵益僊，治中李全叛中山應之。

translations.literal: In the spring of gengchen, the Jin greatly mobilized troops to reinforce Xian; the assistant prefect Li Quan rebelled at Zhongshan in response.
translations.idiomatic: That spring in gengchen, the Jin sent a large relief force to bolster Wu Xian, and Li Quan, the assistant prefect of Zhongshan, defected to join him.

sentences.zh: 俊軍時屯曲陽，僊銳氣來戰，敗之黃山下，僊脫走。

translations.literal: Jun's army was then encamped at Quyang. Xian came with sharp momentum to battle; Jun defeated him beneath Yellow Mountain, and Xian escaped and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's army was then stationed at Quyang. Wu Xian came out eager for battle; Jun routed him below Yellow Mountain, and Wu Xian barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 獻捷于木華黎，由是僊以窮降。

translations.literal: He reported victory to Muqali, and thereby Xian, driven to extremity, surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He presented his victory to Muqali, and as a result Wu Xian, brought to bay, submitted.

sentences.zh: 木華黎承制授俊龍虎衛上將軍、行元帥府事，駐藁城。

translations.literal: Muqali, acting under imperial commission, appointed Jun as General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and provisional administrator of the marshal's headquarters, stationed at Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Acting by imperial commission, Muqali made Jun General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and put him in charge of the marshal's headquarters at Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 俊嘗謁木華黎曰：「武僊黠不可測，終不為我用，請備之。

translations.literal: Jun once paid a visit to Muqali and said: "Wu Xian is cunning and impossible to read; he will never truly serve us. I beg that we guard against him."
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion Jun called on Muqali and said, "Wu Xian is treacherous and unpredictable — he will never be loyal to us. I ask that we take precautions against him."

sentences.zh: 」木華黎然其言，承制授左副元帥。

translations.literal: Muqali approved his words and, by imperial commission, appointed him Left Vice Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali agreed and, by commission, appointed him Left Vice Marshal.

sentences.zh: 陞藁城縣為永安州，號其衆為匡國軍，事一委俊。

translations.literal: Gaocheng County was promoted to Yong'an Prefecture; his followers were styled the Kuangguo Army, and all affairs were entrusted entirely to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Gaocheng County was elevated to Yong'an Prefecture, his troops were named the Army for Restoring the State, and Jun was given full authority over everything there.

sentences.zh: 己酉，僊果殺都元帥史天倪，據真定以叛，旁郡縣皆為僊守。

translations.literal: In jiyou, Xian indeed killed the Grand Marshal Shi Tianni, seized Zhending in rebellion, and neighboring commanderies and counties all became garrisoned for Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In jiyou Wu Xian did indeed kill Grand Marshal Shi Tianni, rebelled from his base at Zhending, and surrounding prefectures and counties all held out for him.

sentences.zh: 俊提孤軍居反側間，戰士不滿千人，拒守永安。

translations.literal: Jun led an isolated army amid disloyal neighbors; his fighting men numbered fewer than a thousand, yet he held Yong'an in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was left with a lone force surrounded by turncoats. With fewer than a thousand soldiers, he still held Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 僊攻之期年，無所利，乃縱兵蹂禾稼，俊呼語之曰：「汝欲得民，而奪之食，無道賊不為也。

translations.literal: Xian besieged it for a full year without profit, then let his troops ravage the grain fields. Jun called out to him: "You wish to win the people, yet you rob them of their food — no bandit without principle would do such a thing."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian besieged the city for a full year without gain, then sent his troops to trample the crops. Jun shouted across to him, "You want to win the people, yet you steal their food — no principled man, not even a bandit, would do that."

sentences.zh: 」僊慚而去，俊出兵掩擊之，僊敗走。

translations.literal: Xian withdrew in shame; Jun sallied forth in a surprise attack, and Xian was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Wu Xian withdrew. Jun then led a surprise attack and put him to rout.

sentences.zh: 久之，俊復夜入真定，僊走死，乃納史天倪弟天澤為帥。

translations.literal: After a long while, Jun again entered Zhending by night. Xian fled to his death, and Jun installed Shi Tianni's younger brother Tianze as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later Jun again entered Zhending by night. Wu Xian fled to his death, and Jun installed Shi Tianni's younger brother Tianze as commander.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，會諸軍圍汴。

translations.literal: In renchen, he joined the combined armies in besieging Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In renchen he joined the allied armies in the siege of Bian.

sentences.zh: 明年，金主棄汴奔歸德，追圍之；

translations.literal: The next year the Jin emperor abandoned Bian and fled to Guide; they pursued and besieged him there.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Jin emperor abandoned Bian and fled to Guide; the allied forces pursued and besieged him there.

sentences.zh: 金兵夜出，薄諸軍於水，俊力戰死焉，時年四十有八。

translations.literal: Jin troops sortied by night and pressed the allied armies at the water's edge. Jun fought with all his strength and died there, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops sortied by night and pressed the allied armies at the water's edge. Jun fought with all his strength and fell there, aged forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 俊早喪父，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Jun lost his father early and was known for filial devotion to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Jun lost his father at an early age and was renowned for his filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 歲時廟祭，非疾病，跪拜必盡禮；

translations.literal: At seasonal temple sacrifices, unless ill, he always performed bowing and kneeling to the full extent of ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: At the seasonal temple sacrifices, unless illness prevented him, he always performed every bow and kneeling to the letter of ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 子雖孩乳，亦使之序拜，曰：「祀，以孝先也，禮宜如是。

translations.literal: Even infants still at the breast he made take their turn in the rites, saying: "Sacrifice begins with filial piety; the ritual ought to be thus."
translations.idiomatic: Even infants still at the breast he made take their turn in the rites, saying, "Sacrifice begins with filial piety — the ritual ought to be observed in just this way."

sentences.zh: 」待族親故人，皆有恩意；

translations.literal: He treated kinsmen and old friends all with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He treated kinsmen and old friends with consistent kindness.

sentences.zh: 里夫家僮，亦接之有道。

translations.literal: Even village laborers and domestic servants he received with proper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Even village laborers and household servants he treated with proper courtesy.

sentences.zh: 克汴時，以侍其軸為賢，延歸教諸子。

translations.literal: When Bian was taken, he considered Shiqi Zhou a man of worth and invited him home to instruct his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian fell, he recognized Shiqi Zhou as a man of talent and invited him home to tutor his sons.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「射，百日事耳；

translations.literal: He once said: "Archery is a matter of a hundred days."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Archery is a hundred days' work.

sentences.zh: 詩、書，非積學不通。

translations.literal: Poetry and the Classics cannot be mastered without long study."
translations.idiomatic: Poetry and the Classics cannot be mastered without years of steady study."

sentences.zh: 」屢誡諸子曰：「吾一農夫耳，遭天下多故，徒以忠義事人，僅立門戶。

translations.literal: He repeatedly admonished his sons: "I am but a farmer who, meeting troubled times, served others only through loyalty and righteousness, barely establishing our household."
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly admonished his sons, "I am nothing but a farmer who, in troubled times, served others through loyalty and righteousness alone, barely establishing our household.

sentences.zh: 深願汝曹力田讀書，勿求非望，為吾累也。」

translations.literal: I deeply hope you will diligently farm and study, seek no improper ambitions, and not bring trouble upon me."
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly hope you will work the fields and study diligently, seek no improper ambitions, and not bring disgrace upon me."

sentences.zh: 俊忠實自許，不為夷險少移，臨陣，勇氣懾衆，立矢石間，怡然若無事，雖中傷亦不為動。

translations.literal: Jun prided himself on steadfast loyalty and was not swayed in the least by ease or peril. In battle his courage awed the host; standing amid arrows and stones he was serene as if nothing were amiss, and even when wounded he did not flinch.
translations.idiomatic: Jun held himself to unwavering loyalty and was unmoved by fortune or adversity. In battle his courage awed the ranks; standing amid flying arrows and stones he remained calm as if nothing were amiss, and even when wounded he did not waver.

sentences.zh: 每慕馬援為人，曰：「馬革裹屍，援固可壯。

translations.literal: He always admired Ma Yuan and said: "To be wrapped in horsehide on the battlefield — how inspiring is Ma Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He always admired Ma Yuan and said, "To be wrapped in horsehide on the battlefield — how inspiring a death Ma Yuan chose.

sentences.zh: 」故戰必持矛先士卒，或諫止之，俊曰：「我人臣也，敵在前，不死，乃趨安脫危乎！

translations.literal: " Therefore in every battle he took spear in hand ahead of the ranks. When some tried to dissuade him, Jun said: "I am a subject of the throne. With the enemy before us, if I do not die fighting, shall I run to safety?
translations.idiomatic: " Accordingly, in every battle he took spear in hand and led from the front. When others tried to dissuade him, Jun said, "I am a subject of the throne. With the enemy before us, if I do not die fighting, shall I run to safety instead!

sentences.zh: 」先是，戊子歲，朝於行在，諸將獻戶口，各增數要利，吏請如衆，俊曰：「民實少而欺以數多，他日上需求無應，必重斂以承命，是我獨利，而民日困也。

translations.literal: Before this, in the wuzi year, when he attended court at the mobile imperial camp, the generals presented household registers, each inflating the numbers for profit. The clerks asked that he follow the crowd. Jun said: "The people are in truth few, yet we deceive by reporting more. Later when requisitions come there will be nothing to meet them, and they will surely levy heavy taxes to fulfill the command — we alone profit while the people grow ever poorer."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the wuzi year, when he attended court at the imperial camp, the generals submitted household registers, each inflating the numbers for profit. The clerks asked him to do likewise. Jun said, "The people are in truth fewer than we report. When requisitions come later and there is nothing to meet them, heavy levies will be imposed to satisfy the command — we alone profit while the people grow ever poorer."

sentences.zh: 」行元帥府時，狂男子三百餘人期日作亂，事覺，戮其渠魁，餘並釋之。

translations.literal: While administering the marshal's headquarters, more than three hundred madmen plotted rebellion on a fixed day. When the plot was discovered, he executed the ringleaders and released the rest.
translations.idiomatic: While administering the marshal's headquarters, more than three hundred madmen plotted a rebellion on a fixed day. When the plot was discovered, he executed the ringleaders and released the rest.

sentences.zh: 深、冀間妖人惑衆，圖為不軌，連逮者數萬人，有司議當族，俊力請主者，但誅首惡。

translations.literal: Sorcerers between Shen and Ji deluded the masses and plotted sedition; tens of thousands were implicated. The officials proposed exterminating entire clans, but Jun strongly pleaded with the chief official that only the chief evildoers be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Sorcerers between Shen and Ji deluded the masses and plotted sedition; tens of thousands were implicated. The officials proposed exterminating entire clans, but Jun strongly pleaded with the chief official to execute only the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 永安節度使劉成叛降武僊於威州，俊下令曰：「逆者一人，餘能去逆，即忠義士，與其家財，仍奏官之。

translations.literal: Liu Cheng, military commissioner of Yong'an, rebelled and surrendered to Wu Xian at Weizhou. Jun issued an order: "There is but one traitor. Any who can abandon rebellion will be counted loyal and heroic; their family property shall be restored and they shall be recommended for office."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cheng, military commissioner of Yong'an, rebelled and surrendered to Wu Xian at Weizhou. Jun issued an order: "There is but one traitor. Any who abandon rebellion will be counted loyal and heroic; their family property shall be restored and they shall be recommended for office."

sentences.zh: 」衆果去成降。

translations.literal: The troops indeed abandoned Cheng and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The troops indeed abandoned Liu Cheng and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 沃州民寨天臺為盜，既破降之，他將利其子女，欲掠之，俊曰：「城降而俘其家，仁者不為也。

translations.literal: The people of Wozhou had fortified Tiantai as bandits. After they were defeated and surrendered, other commanders coveted their women and children and wished to seize them. Jun said: "When a city submits, to take its people captive — no man of humanity would do that."
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wozhou had fortified Tiantai and turned to banditry. After they were defeated and submitted, other commanders coveted their women and children and wished to seize them. Jun said, "When a city submits, to take its families captive — no man of humanity would do that."

sentences.zh: 」衆義不取。

translations.literal: The troops, moved by righteousness, did not take them.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his words, the troops refrained from taking them.

sentences.zh: 南征時，人多歸俊願為奴者，既全其家，歸悉縱為民。

translations.literal: During the southern campaign many people came to Jun wishing to become his slaves. After he had preserved their families whole, upon returning he released them all as free commoners.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern campaign many people came to Jun offering themselves as slaves. After he had kept their families intact, upon returning he released them all as free commoners.

sentences.zh: 鄰境人有被掠賣者，亦與直贖還之。

translations.literal: People in neighboring territories who had been seized and sold he also redeemed at fair price and returned.
translations.idiomatic: People in neighboring territories who had been seized and sold he also redeemed at fair price and sent home.

sentences.zh: 其天性之美類如此。

translations.literal: His innate goodness was of this kind throughout.
translations.idiomatic: His innate goodness showed itself in ways such as these.

sentences.zh: 俊器度弘遠，善戰而不妄殺，故人樂為之用。

translations.literal: Jun's breadth of mind was far-reaching; he was skilled in battle yet did not kill recklessly, so men were glad to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's breadth of mind was far-reaching. He was skilled in battle yet did not kill recklessly, and men were glad to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 大小百戰，無不克捷。

translations.literal: In a hundred battles great and small, none went without victory.
translations.idiomatic: In a hundred battles great and small, he never failed to prevail.

sentences.zh: 為政寬明，見人善治田廬，必召與歡語，有惰者，則怒罰之，故其部完實，民惟恐其去也。

translations.literal: In governance he was lenient and clear-sighted. When he saw someone who managed fields and homesteads well, he always summoned him for friendly conversation; when there were the lazy, he punished them in anger. Therefore his district was complete and solid, and the people feared only that he might leave.
translations.idiomatic: In governance he was lenient and clear-sighted. When he saw someone who managed fields and homesteads well, he always summoned him for friendly conversation; the lazy he punished sternly. His district therefore remained prosperous and intact, and the people feared only that he might leave.

sentences.zh: 贈翊運效節功臣、太傅、開府儀同三司、上柱國，封壽國公，諡忠烈。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister for Supporting the Dynasty and Maintaining Integrity in Adversity, Grand Tutor, Honorary Grand Counselor with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, Supreme Pillar of the State; enfeoffed as Duke of Shou; posthumous name Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister for Supporting the Dynasty and Maintaining Integrity in Adversity, Grand Tutor, Honorary Grand Counselor with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, and Supreme Pillar of the State; enfeoffed as Duke of Shou; posthumous name Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 加贈推忠翊運效節功臣、太傅、開府儀同三司、上柱國，改封趙國公。

translations.literal: He was further posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister for Loyalty, Support of the Dynasty, and Integrity in Adversity, Grand Tutor, Honorary Grand Counselor with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, Supreme Pillar of the State; re-enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was further posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister for Loyalty, Support of the Dynasty, and Integrity in Adversity, Grand Tutor, Honorary Grand Counselor with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, and Supreme Pillar of the State; re-enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 子文炳、文蔚、文用、文直、文忠，文炳自有傳。

translations.literal: His sons were Wenbing, Wenyue, Wenyong, Wenzhi, and Wenzhong; Wenbing has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Wenbing, Wenyue, Wenyong, Wenzhi, and Wenzhong; Wenbing has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 文蔚字彥華，俊之次子也。

translations.literal: Wenyue, courtesy name Yanhua, was Jun's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyue, styled Yanhua, was Dong Jun's second son.

sentences.zh: 重厚寡言，不事嬉戲，立志勤苦，讀書忘倦。

translations.literal: He was grave and taciturn, did not engage in play, set his will on diligence and hardship, and read books without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: Grave and taciturn, he shunned idle play, devoted himself to hard work, and read without ever growing weary.

sentences.zh: 及長，善騎射，膂力絕人。

translations.literal: When grown, he was skilled at mounted archery and his physical strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, he was skilled at riding and archery, and his physical strength surpassed that of ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 事母至孝，接人謙恭，凡所與交，貴賤長幼，待之無異；

translations.literal: He was utterly filial to his mother and humble in receiving others. All with whom he associated, high or low, elder or younger, he treated without distinction.
translations.idiomatic: He was utterly filial toward his mother and humble in his dealings with others. All whom he knew, whether high or low, elder or younger, he treated without distinction.

sentences.zh: 至於一揖，必正容端體，俛首幾至于地，徐徐起拱，人所難能。

translations.literal: Even in a single bow he always composed his face and straightened his body, bowed his head nearly to the ground, and slowly rose with hands clasped — what others found difficult to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Even in a single bow he always composed his face and straightened his posture, bowed his head nearly to the ground, and slowly rose with hands clasped — a courtesy few could match.

sentences.zh: 兄文炳為藁城令，厲精於政，家務悉委之，凡供給祭祀賓客之事，無不盡心。

translations.literal: His elder brother Wenbing was magistrate of Gaocheng and applied himself zealously to governance; all household affairs were entrusted to Wenyue, and in every matter of supplying sacrifices and receiving guests he gave his utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Wenbing served as magistrate of Gaocheng and applied himself zealously to governance; all household affairs were entrusted to Wenyue, who devoted himself wholeheartedly to every matter of sacrifice and hospitality.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，起民兵南征，文炳命文蔚率十有七人，私整鞍馬衣甲，自為一隊，與衆軍渡淮。

translations.literal: In xinchou, militia were raised for the southern campaign. Wenbing ordered Wenyue to lead seventeen men, privately prepare saddles, horses, clothing, and armor, form a separate unit, and cross the Huai with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: In xinchou, when militia were raised for the southern campaign, Wenbing ordered Wenyue to lead seventeen men, privately outfit saddles, horses, clothing, and armor, form an independent unit, and cross the Huai with the main army.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，世祖收大理，還駐六盤山。

translations.literal: In jiayin, Kublai conquered Dali and returned to encamp at Liupan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In jiayin, Kublai conquered Dali and returned to encamp at Liupan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 文炳以文蔚孝謹公勤，可委以事，解所佩金符以讓，帝嘉賞之，授藁城等處行軍千戶。

translations.literal: Wenbing, considering Wenyue filial, careful, fair, and diligent, fit to be entrusted with affairs, removed the golden tally he wore and yielded it to him. The emperor praised and rewarded this, appointing Wenyue as mobile chiliarch of Gaocheng and neighboring districts.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing, considering Wenyue filial, careful, fair, and diligent, fit to be entrusted with responsibility, removed the golden tally he wore and yielded it to him. The emperor praised and rewarded this, appointing Wenyue mobile chiliarch of Gaocheng and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 南鎮鄧州，與荊、襄接境，沿邊城壁未築。

translations.literal: He was stationed in the south at Dengzhou, bordering Jing and Xiang; along the frontier the city walls had not yet been built.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to the south at Dengzhou, on the border with Jing and Xiang, where the frontier walls had not yet been built.

sentences.zh: 是年冬十一月，修光化；

translations.literal: That year in the eleventh month of winter he repaired Guanghua.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the eleventh month, he repaired Guanghua.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，立毗陽；

translations.literal: In yimao, he established Piyang.
translations.idiomatic: In yimao he established Piyang.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，築棗陽。

translations.literal: In bingchen, he built Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In bingchen he built Zaoyang.

sentences.zh: 文蔚悉緫之，治板幹，具畚鍤，儲餱糧，運木石，程其工力，時其饑飽，藥其疾病，見執役者，常以善言撫之，弗事威猛。

translations.literal: Wenyue supervised all of this: prepared planks and timbers, supplied hoes and shovels, stored dry rations, transported wood and stone, measured out labor, timed meals, tended the sick, and whenever he saw those under corvée labor always comforted them with kind words, never relying on harsh severity.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyue supervised all of this: prepared planks and timbers, supplied hoes and shovels, stored dry rations, transported wood and stone, measured out labor, timed meals, tended the sick, and whenever he saw those under corvée labor always comforted them with kind words, never relying on harsh severity.

sentences.zh: 衆咸感曰：「他將領役，鞭箠怒辱，不恤困苦。

translations.literal: All were moved and said: "Other commanders leading corvée labor whip and insult in anger, caring nothing for hardship.
translations.idiomatic: All were deeply moved and said, "Other commanders leading corvée labor whip and insult in anger, caring nothing for hardship.

sentences.zh: 今董侯慈惠若此，我曹安忍負之。

translations.literal: Now Lord Dong is so kind and gracious — how could we bear to fail him.
translations.idiomatic: Now Lord Dong is so kind and gracious — how could we bear to fail him.

sentences.zh: 」各盡力成之。

translations.literal: " Each gave his utmost to complete the work.
translations.idiomatic: " Each gave his utmost to complete the work.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，攻襄，樊城南據漢江，北阻湖水，卒不得渡。

translations.literal: In dingsi, they attacked Xiang. Fancheng lay south on the Han River and was blocked to the north by lake waters; in the end they could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: In dingsi they attacked Xiang. Fancheng lay south on the Han River with lake waters blocking the north; in the end they could not cross.

sentences.zh: 文蔚夜領兵士，於湖水狹隘之處，伐木拔根，立於水，實以薪草為橋梁，頃之即成，至曉，師悉渡，圍已合，城中大驚異之。

translations.literal: Wenyue led soldiers by night to a narrow place in the lake waters, felled trees and pulled up roots, set them upright in the water, packed them with firewood and grass to make a bridge, and in no time it was complete. By dawn the army had all crossed, the encirclement was closed, and the city was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyue led soldiers by night to a narrow stretch of the lake, felled trees and pulled up roots, set them upright in the water, and packed them with firewood and grass to make a bridge. In no time it was complete; by dawn the army had all crossed, the encirclement was closed, and the city was greatly astonished.

sentences.zh: 文蔚復統拔都軍以當前行，奪其外城，論功居最。

translations.literal: Wenyue again commanded the Badu army as the vanguard, seized the outer city, and in reckoning merit ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyue again commanded the Badu army as the vanguard, seized the outer city, and ranked first when merit was reckoned.

sentences.zh: 己未，憲宗伐宋，入川蜀，文蔚奉詔，將鄧之選兵西上，由褒斜歷劍閣，而劍、閬諸州，平地不能守，置州事於山。

translations.literal: In jiwei, Möngke attacked Song and entered Chuan-Shu. Wenyue, by imperial order, led Deng's selected troops westward, passing through Baoxie and traversing Jian'ge. In the prefectures of Jian and Lang, the flat land could not be held, so prefectural administration was placed in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei, when Möngke attacked Song and entered Chuan-Shu, Wenyue, by imperial order, led Deng's selected troops westward through Baoxie and over Jian'ge. In the prefectures of Jian and Lang the flat land could not be held, so prefectural administration was placed in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 師行大獲、雲頂、長寧、苦竹諸寨，長驅而前，至釣魚山，崖壁巉峭，惟一徑可登，恃險阻未即降。

translations.literal: The army marched through the stockades of Dahuo, Yunding, Changning, and Kuzhu, driving straight forward to Diaoyu Mountain. Its cliffs were steep and sheer; only one path could be climbed. Relying on the perilous terrain, they did not immediately submit.
translations.idiomatic: The army marched through the stockades of Dahuo, Yunding, Changning, and Kuzhu and drove straight forward to Diaoyu Mountain. Its cliffs were steep and sheer, with only one path to the top; relying on the terrain, the defenders did not immediately submit.

sentences.zh: 帝命攻之，文蔚以次往攻，迺激厲將士，挾雲梯，冒飛石，履崎嶇以登，直抵其寨苦戰，頃之，兵士被傷，迺還。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered an assault. Wenyue took his turn to attack, then roused the officers and soldiers, carrying scaling ladders, braving flying stones, treading rugged paths to climb, and pressing straight to the stockade in bitter fighting. Before long soldiers were wounded, and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an assault. Wenyue took his turn to attack, roused his officers and soldiers, carried scaling ladders, braved flying stones, and climbed the rugged path straight to the stockade in bitter fighting. Before long his soldiers were wounded, and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝親見之，加以賞賚。

translations.literal: The emperor saw this in person and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor witnessed this in person and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，世祖置武衛軍，文蔚以鄧兵入為千戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong, Kublai established the Martial Guard Army; Wenyue entered it with his Deng troops as chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong, Kublai established the Martial Guard Army; Wenyue entered it with his Deng troops as chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 帝北狩，留屯上都。

translations.literal: When the emperor hunted north, Wenyue remained garrisoned at Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went north on campaign, Wenyue remained garrisoned at Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 三年，李璮反，據濟南，文蔚以麾下軍圍其南面，春秋力戰，城破璮誅，奏功還。

translations.literal: In the third year, Li Tan rebelled and held Jinan. Wenyue with his subordinate army besieged its southern face, fighting through spring and autumn with all his strength. When the city fell Tan was executed; Wenyue reported merit and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Li Tan rebelled and held Jinan. Wenyue with his subordinate army besieged its southern face, fighting through spring and autumn with all his strength. When the city fell Tan was executed; Wenyue reported his merit and returned.

sentences.zh: 至元五年七月十七日，以疾卒于上都之炭山。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day of the seventh month in the fifth year of Zhiyuan, he died of illness at Tanshan in Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day of the seventh month in the fifth year of Zhiyuan, he died of illness at Tanshan in Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 弟文忠，時為樞密僉院，乞護喪南還，帝甚憫之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wenzhong, then associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, begged to escort the coffin south; the emperor was deeply moved with compassion.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wenzhong, then associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, begged to escort the coffin south; the emperor was deeply moved with compassion.

sentences.zh: 泰定中，贈明威將軍、僉右衛使司事、上騎都尉、隴西郡伯。

translations.literal: During the Taiding era he was posthumously granted Bright Might General, associate director of the Right Guard Commission, Supreme Cavalry Commandant, and Baron of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiding era he was posthumously granted Bright Might General, associate director of the Right Guard Commission, Supreme Cavalry Commandant, and Baron of Longxi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 文用字彥材，俊之第三子也。

translations.literal: Wenyong, courtesy name Yancai, was Jun's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong, styled Yancai, was Dong Jun's third son.

sentences.zh: 生十歲，父死，長兄文炳教諸弟有法。

translations.literal: At ten years of age his father died; his eldest brother Wenbing instructed his younger brothers with proper method.
translations.idiomatic: When he was ten his father died; his eldest brother Wenbing instructed his younger brothers with proper discipline.

sentences.zh: 文用學問早成，弱冠試詞賦中選。

translations.literal: Wenyong's learning matured early; at the capping age he tested in rhapsody and prose and was selected.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong's learning matured early; at the capping age he tested in rhapsody and prose and was selected.

sentences.zh: 時以真定藁城奉莊聖太后湯沐，庚戌，太后命擇邑中子弟來上，文用始從文炳謁太后于和林城。

translations.literal: At that time Zhending's Gaocheng was assigned as bath-and-income lands for Empress Dowager Zhuang Sheng. In gengxu the empress dowager ordered that select youths of the district be sent up; Wenyong first followed Wenbing to pay court to the empress dowager at Helin city.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gaocheng in Zhending was assigned as bath-and-income lands for Empress Dowager Zhuang Sheng. In gengxu the empress dowager ordered select youths of the district sent up; Wenyong first followed Wenbing to pay court to the empress dowager at Helin.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛藩，命文用主文書，講說帳中，常見許重。

translations.literal: Kublai, while still heir apparent, ordered Wenyong to manage documents and lecture within his tent; he was often granted special esteem.
translations.idiomatic: While Kublai was still heir apparent, he ordered Wenyong to manage documents and lecture within his tent; he was often granted special esteem.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，世祖受命憲宗自河西征雲南大理。

translations.literal: In guichou, Kublai received Möngke's commission to campaign from Hexi against Yunnan and Dali.
translations.idiomatic: In guichou, Kublai received Möngke's commission to campaign from Hexi against Yunnan and Dali.

sentences.zh: 文用與弟文忠從軍，督糧械，贊軍務。

translations.literal: Wenyong and his younger brother Wenzhong followed the army, supervising grain and equipment and assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong and his younger brother Wenzhong followed the army, supervising grain and equipment and assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，世祖令授皇子經，是為北平王、雲南王也。

translations.literal: In dingsi, Kublai ordered him to instruct the princes in the classics — these were the Prince of Beiping and the Prince of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In dingsi, Kublai ordered him to instruct the princes in the classics — these were the Prince of Beiping and the Prince of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 又命召遺老竇默、姚樞、李俊民、李冶、魏璠於四方。

translations.literal: He also ordered that surviving elders — Dou Mo, Yao Shu, Li Junmin, Li Ye, and Wei Fan — be summoned from the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered that surviving elders — Dou Mo, Yao Shu, Li Junmin, Li Ye, and Wei Fan — be summoned from across the realm.

sentences.zh: 己未，伐宋，文用發沿邊蒙古、漢人諸軍，理軍需。

translations.literal: In jiwei, when they attacked Song, Wenyong mobilized Mongol and Han armies along the frontier and managed military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei, when they attacked Song, Wenyong mobilized Mongol and Han armies along the frontier and managed military supplies.

sentences.zh: 將攻鄂州，宋賈似道、呂文德將兵來拒，水陸軍容甚盛。

translations.literal: About to attack Ezhou, Song's Jia Sidao and Lu Wende led troops to resist; their land and water forces were very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: As they prepared to attack Ezhou, Song's Jia Sidao and Lu Wende led troops to resist; their land and water forces were very imposing.

sentences.zh: 九月，世祖臨江閱戰，文炳求先進戰，文用與文忠固請偕行，世祖親料甲冑，擇大艦授之，大破宋師。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Kublai reviewed the battle from the riverbank. Wenbing asked to advance and fight first; Wenyong and Wenzhong firmly begged to go together. Kublai personally fitted out armor, selected a large warship, and gave it to them; they greatly defeated the Song army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Kublai reviewed the battle from the riverbank. Wenbing asked to advance and fight first; Wenyong and Wenzhong firmly begged to go together. Kublai personally fitted out their armor, selected a large warship, and gave it to them; they routed the Song army.

sentences.zh: 至元改元，召為西夏中興等路行省郎中。

translations.literal: When the Zhiyuan era began, he was summoned as director of the Branch Secretariat of Zhongxing and other circuits in Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhiyuan era began, he was summoned as director of the Branch Secretariat of Zhongxing and other circuits in Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 中興自渾都海之亂，民間相恐動，竄匿山谷。

translations.literal: Since the turmoil of Hulagu in Zhongxing, the common people had been mutually alarmed and hid themselves in mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Since the turmoil of Hulagu in Zhongxing, the common people had been mutually alarmed and hid themselves in mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 文用至，鎮之以靜，乃為書置通衢諭之，民乃安。

translations.literal: When Wenyong arrived, he calmed them with stillness, then wrote proclamations and placed them at crossroads to instruct them, and the people were reassured.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyong arrived, he calmed them with quiet authority, then posted proclamations at crossroads to instruct them, and the people were reassured.

sentences.zh: 始開唐來、漢延、秦家等渠，墾中興、西涼、甘、肅、瓜、沙等州之土為水田若干，於是民之歸者戶四五萬，悉授田種，頒農具；

translations.literal: He began to open the canals of Tanglai, Hanyan, Qinjia, and others, and reclaimed land in Zhongxing, Xiliang, Gan, Su, Gua, Sha, and other prefectures as paddy fields in considerable measure. Thereupon returning households numbered forty or fifty thousand; all were granted seed and farm implements were distributed.
translations.idiomatic: He began to open the canals of Tanglai, Hanyan, Qinjia, and others, and reclaimed land in Zhongxing, Xiliang, Gan, Su, Gua, Sha, and other prefectures as paddy fields. Returning households numbered forty or fifty thousand; all were granted seed and farm implements.

sentences.zh: 更造舟置黃河中，受諸部落及潰叛之來降者。

translations.literal: He further built boats and placed them on the Yellow River to receive tribes and those who came to surrender after defeat or rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He further built boats and placed them on the Yellow River to receive tribes and those who came to surrender after defeat or rebellion.

sentences.zh: 時諸王只必鐵木兒鎮西方，其下縱橫，需索無筭，省臣不能支，文用坐幕府，輒面折以法。

translations.literal: At that time the prince Zhibi Temür held the west; his subordinates ran rampant, their demands beyond counting, and the provincial officials could not sustain them. Wenyong sat in the marshal's headquarters and repeatedly rebuked them to their faces according to law.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Zhibi Temür held the western frontier; his subordinates ran rampant, their demands beyond counting, and the provincial officials could not sustain them. Wenyong served in the marshal's headquarters and repeatedly rebuked them to their faces according to law.

sentences.zh: 其徒積忿，譖文用於王，王怒，召文用，使左右雜問之，意叵測。

translations.literal: His followers nursed resentment and slandered Wenyong to the prince. The prince grew angry, summoned Wenyong, and had his attendants question him in mixed fashion; his intent was impossible to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: His followers nursed their resentment and slandered Wenyong to the prince. The prince grew angry, summoned Wenyong, and had his attendants question him in confused fashion; his intent was impossible to fathom.

sentences.zh: 文用曰：「我天子命吏，非汝等所當問，請得與天子所遣為王傅者辨之。

translations.literal: Wenyong said: "I am an officer appointed by the Son of Heaven; this is not for you to question. I ask to debate the matter with the tutor the Son of Heaven sent to serve the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong said, "I am an officer appointed by the Son of Heaven; this is not for you to question. I ask to debate the matter with the tutor the Son of Heaven sent to serve the prince.

sentences.zh: 」王即遣其傅訊文用。

translations.literal: " The prince thereupon sent his tutor to examine Wenyong.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince thereupon sent his tutor to examine Wenyong.

sentences.zh: 其傅中朝舊臣，不肯順王意。

translations.literal: His tutor was a former minister of the central court and would not comply with the prince's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: His tutor was a former minister of the central court and would not comply with the prince's wishes.

sentences.zh: 文用謂之曰：「我漢人，生死不足計。

translations.literal: Wenyong said to him: "I am a Han Chinese; life and death are not worth reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong said to him, "I am a Han Chinese; life and death are not worth reckoning.

sentences.zh: 所恨者，仁慈寬厚如王，以重戚鎮遠方，而其下毒虐百姓，凌暴官府，傷王威名，於事體不便。

translations.literal: What I regret is that a prince as benevolent and generous as you, stationed in a distant region by virtue of imperial kinship, has subordinates who cruelly abuse the common people and bully the government offices, harming your prestige and making matters impracticable.
translations.idiomatic: What I regret is that a prince as benevolent and generous as you, stationed in a distant region by virtue of imperial kinship, has subordinates who cruelly abuse the common people and bully the government offices, harming your prestige and making matters impracticable.

sentences.zh: 」因歷指其不法者數十事，其傅驚起，去白王，王即召文用謝之曰：「非郎中，我殆不知。

translations.literal: " He then enumerated dozens of their unlawful acts. The tutor started up in alarm, went to report to the prince, and the prince immediately summoned Wenyong and apologized, saying: "Had it not been for the Director, I would almost not have known.
translations.idiomatic: " He then enumerated dozens of their unlawful acts. The tutor started up in alarm, went to report to the prince, and the prince immediately summoned Wenyong and apologized, saying, "Had it not been for the Director, I would almost not have known.

sentences.zh: 郎中持此心事朝廷，宜勿怠。

translations.literal: Director, hold this intent in your heart on behalf of the court, and do not slacken.
translations.idiomatic: Director, hold this intent in your heart on behalf of the court, and do not slacken.

sentences.zh: 」自是譖不行而省府事頗立。

translations.literal: " From then on slander did not prevail, and the affairs of the provincial government were largely established.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on slander did not prevail, and the affairs of the provincial government were largely established.

sentences.zh: 二年，入奏經略事宜還，以上旨行之，中興遂定。

translations.literal: In the second year he entered court to report on frontier strategy and returned; he carried out the imperial will, and Zhongxing was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he entered court to report on frontier strategy and returned; he carried out the imperial will, and Zhongxing was thereby settled.

sentences.zh: 八年，立司農司，授山東東西道巡行勸農使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Office of the Directors of Agriculture was established, and he was appointed itinerant commissioner for encouraging agriculture in the Eastern and Western Circuits of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Office of the Directors of Agriculture was established, and he was appointed itinerant commissioner for encouraging agriculture in the Eastern and Western Circuits of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 山東自更叛亂，野多曠土，文用巡行勸勵，無間幽僻。

translations.literal: Shandong, since repeated rebellions, had much wasteland in the countryside. Wenyong toured the region encouraging and exhorting, sparing neither remote nor secluded places.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong, since repeated rebellions, had much wasteland in the countryside. Wenyong toured the region encouraging and exhorting, sparing neither remote nor secluded places.

sentences.zh: 入登州境，見其墾辟有方，以郡守移剌某為能，作詩表異之。

translations.literal: Entering the territory of Dengzhou, he saw that reclamation and cultivation there were well ordered; he considered the prefect Yelü Mou capable and composed a poem to mark his distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the territory of Dengzhou, he saw that reclamation and cultivation there were well ordered; he considered the prefect Yelü Mou capable and composed a poem to mark his distinction.

sentences.zh: 於是列郡咸勸，地利畢興，五年之間，政績為天下勸農使之最。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the commanderies were alike encouraged, and the productive capacity of the land was fully revived. Within five years his administrative achievements ranked first among all the commissioners for encouraging agriculture in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all the commanderies were alike encouraged, and the productive capacity of the land was fully revived. Within five years his administrative achievements ranked first among all the commissioners for encouraging agriculture in the realm.

sentences.zh: 十二年，丞相安童奏文用為工部侍郎，代紇石里。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Chancellor Antong memorialized that Wenyong be made vice minister of the Ministry of Works, replacing Heshili.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Chancellor Antong memorialized that Wenyong be made vice minister of the Ministry of Works, replacing Heshili.

sentences.zh: 紇石里，阿合馬私人也。

translations.literal: Heshili was Ahmad's private man.
translations.idiomatic: Heshili was Ahmad's private man.

sentences.zh: 其徒既讒間安童罷相，即使鷹監奏曰：「自紇石里去，工部侍郎不給鷹食，鷹且瘦死。

translations.literal: His followers, having already slandered Antong until he was removed as chancellor, then had the hawk keeper memorialize, saying: "Since Heshili left, the vice minister of Works has not supplied hawk food, and the hawks will soon starve to death.
translations.idiomatic: His followers, having already slandered Antong until he was removed as chancellor, then had the hawk keeper memorialize, saying, "Since Heshili left, the vice minister of Works has not supplied hawk food, and the hawks will soon starve to death.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，促召治之，因急捕文用入見，帝望見曰：「董文用乃為爾治鷹食者耶！

translations.literal: " The emperor grew angry and urgently summoned him for punishment; he then had Wenyong seized and brought in for audience. When the emperor saw him from afar he said: "Is Dong Wenyong the one who feeds your hawks!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor grew angry and urgently summoned him for punishment; he then had Wenyong seized and brought in for audience. When the emperor saw him from afar he said, "Is Dong Wenyong the one who feeds your hawks!

sentences.zh: 」置不問，別令取給有司。

translations.literal: " He set the matter aside without inquiry and separately ordered the relevant offices to provide supplies.
translations.idiomatic: " He set the matter aside without inquiry and separately ordered the relevant offices to provide supplies.

sentences.zh: 十三年，出文用為衛輝路緫管，佩金虎符。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Wenyong was sent out as superintendent of Weihui Circuit and wore the golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Wenyong was sent out as superintendent of Weihui Circuit and wore the golden tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 郡當衝要，民為兵者十之九，餘皆單弱貧病，不堪力役。

translations.literal: The commandery lay on a vital route; nine tenths of the people were soldiers, and the rest were all solitary, weak, poor, or sick, unable to bear corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery lay on a vital route; nine tenths of the people were soldiers, and the rest were all solitary, weak, poor, or sick, unable to bear corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 會初得江南，圖籍、金玉、財帛之運，日夜不絕于道，警衛輸輓，日役數千夫。

translations.literal: It happened that the south had just been taken; transport of registers, gold and jade, and wealth and silks never ceased day or night on the roads, and for guard duty and transport several thousand laborers were impressed each day.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the south had just been taken; transport of registers, gold and jade, and wealth and silks never ceased day or night on the roads, and for guard duty and transport several thousand laborers were impressed each day.

sentences.zh: 文用憂之曰：「吾民弊矣，而又重妨耕作，殆不可。

translations.literal: Wenyong worried over this and said: "Our people are exhausted, and this further greatly obstructs farming — it is almost impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong worried over this and said, "Our people are exhausted, and this further greatly obstructs farming — it is almost impossible.

sentences.zh: 」乃從轉運主者言：「州縣吏卒，足以備用，不必重煩吾民也。

translations.literal: " He then spoke to the head of transport, saying: "The clerks and soldiers of the prefectures and counties are sufficient for use; there is no need to burden our people again.
translations.idiomatic: " He then spoke to the head of transport, saying, "The clerks and soldiers of the prefectures and counties are sufficient for the task; there is no need to burden our people again.

sentences.zh: 」主者曰：「汝言誠然，萬一有不虞，則罪將誰歸！

translations.literal: " The head said: "What you say is indeed so, but if by any chance something goes wrong, to whom will the blame fall!
translations.idiomatic: " The head said, "What you say is indeed so, but if by any chance something goes wrong, to whom will the blame fall!

sentences.zh: 」文用即手書具官姓名保任之。

translations.literal: " Wenyong immediately wrote out in his own hand the full names and offices of those who would guarantee the undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenyong immediately wrote out in his own hand the full names and offices of those who would guarantee the undertaking.

sentences.zh: 民得以時耕，而運事亦不廢。

translations.literal: The people were able to farm on schedule, and transport work was not abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The people were able to farm on schedule, and transport work was not abandoned.

sentences.zh: 諸郡運江淮粟于京師，衛當運十五萬石，文用曰：「民籍可役者無幾，且江淮風水，舟不能以時至，而先為期會，是未運而民已困矣。

translations.literal: The commanderies transported grain from the Jianghuai region to the capital; Weihui was to transport one hundred fifty thousand shi. Wenyong said: "Among those on the household registers fit for corvée there are few, and moreover the winds and waters of the Jianghuai prevent boats from arriving on time; yet deadlines are set in advance — before transport even begins the people are already exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The commanderies transported grain from the Jianghuai region to the capital; Weihui was to transport one hundred fifty thousand shi. Wenyong said, "Among those on the household registers fit for corvée there are few, and moreover the winds and waters of the Jianghuai prevent boats from arriving on time; yet deadlines are set in advance — before transport even begins the people are already exhausted.

sentences.zh: 」乃集旁郡通議，立驛置法，民力以舒。

translations.literal: " He then gathered neighboring commanderies for joint consultation, established relay-station regulations, and the people's labor was eased.
translations.idiomatic: " He then gathered neighboring commanderies for joint consultation, established relay-station regulations, and the people's labor was eased.

sentences.zh: 十四年，詣汴漕司言事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he went to the Bian grain-transport office to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he went to the Bian grain-transport office to discuss affairs.

sentences.zh: 適漕司議通沁水北東合流御河以便漕者，文用曰：「衛為郡，地最下，大雨時行，沁水輒溢出百十里間；

translations.literal: It happened that the transport office was debating opening a channel for the Qin River's northern and eastern branches to join the Imperial Canal to facilitate transport. Wenyong said: "Weihui as a commandery lies at the lowest ground; when heavy rains come, the Qin River always overflows across a hundred or more li;
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the transport office was debating opening a channel for the Qin River's northern and eastern branches to join the Imperial Canal to facilitate transport. Wenyong said, "Weihui as a commandery lies at the lowest ground; when heavy rains come, the Qin River always overflows across a hundred or more li;

sentences.zh: 雨更甚，水不得達于河，即浸淫及衛，今又引之使來，豈惟無衛，將無大名、長蘆矣。

translations.literal: when the rain grows heavier still and the water cannot reach the river, it spreads and reaches Weihui. Now you would also draw it here — will there be not only no Weihui, but soon no Daming or Changlu either?
translations.idiomatic: when the rain grows heavier still and the water cannot reach the river, it spreads and reaches Weihui. Now you would also draw it here — will there be not only no Weihui, but soon no Daming or Changlu either?

sentences.zh: 」會朝廷遣使相地形，上言：「衛州城中浮屠最高者，纔與沁水平，勢不可開也。

translations.literal: " It happened that the court sent envoys to survey the terrain, and they memorialized: "The tallest pagoda in Weizhou city is only level with the Qin River; by its configuration the channel cannot be opened.
translations.idiomatic: " It happened that the court sent envoys to survey the terrain, and they memorialized, "The tallest pagoda in Weizhou city is only level with the Qin River; by its configuration the channel cannot be opened.

sentences.zh: 」事遂寢。

translations.literal: " The matter was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter was thereupon dropped.

sentences.zh: 十六年，受代歸田里，茅茨數椽，僅避風雨，讀書賦詩，怡然燕居。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he completed his term and returned to his fields; a thatched hut of a few rafters barely kept off wind and rain. He read books and composed poetry, dwelling at ease in contentment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he completed his term and returned to his fields; a thatched hut of a few rafters barely kept off wind and rain. He read books and composed poetry, dwelling at ease in contentment.

sentences.zh: 裕宗在東宮，數為臺臣言：「董文用勳舊忠良，何以不見用！

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhenjin (Yuzong), in the Eastern Palace, repeatedly said to the censorial officials: "Dong Wenyong is a meritorious elder and a loyal man — why is he not employed!
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhenjin (Yuzong), in the Eastern Palace, repeatedly said to the censorial officials, "Dong Wenyong is a meritorious elder and a loyal man — why is he not employed!

sentences.zh: 」十八年，臺臣奏起文用為山北遼東道提刑按察使，不赴。

translations.literal: " In the eighteenth year the censorial officials memorialized to recall Wenyong as intendant and surveillance commissioner of the Shanbei Liaodong Circuit; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eighteenth year the censorial officials memorialized to recall Wenyong as intendant and surveillance commissioner of the Shanbei Liaodong Circuit; he did not go.

sentences.zh: 十九年，朝廷選用舊臣，召文用為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the court selected former ministers for office and summoned Wenyong as minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the court selected former ministers for office and summoned Wenyong as minister of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 自是朝廷有大議，未嘗不與聞。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever the court had major deliberations, he was never left uninformed.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever the court had major deliberations, he was never left uninformed.

sentences.zh: 二十年，江淮省臣有欲專肆而忌廉察官，建議行臺隸行省，狀上，集朝臣議之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year provincial officials of the Jianghuai region, wishing to act without restraint and resenting the integrity-inspecting officers, proposed subordinating the supervisory Branch Secretariat to the provincial Branch Secretariat. The proposal was submitted, and the court ministers were assembled to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year provincial officials of the Jianghuai region, wishing to act without restraint and resenting the integrity-inspecting officers, proposed subordinating the supervisory Branch Secretariat to the provincial Branch Secretariat. The proposal was submitted, and the court ministers were assembled to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 文用議曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Wenyong argued: "This cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong argued, "This cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 御史臺，譬之卧虎，雖未噬人，人猶畏其為虎也。

translations.literal: The Censorate is like a crouching tiger: though it has not yet bitten anyone, people still fear it as a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate is like a crouching tiger: though it has not yet bitten anyone, people still fear it as a tiger.

sentences.zh: 今虛名僅存，紀綱猶不振，一旦摧抑之，則風采薾然，無可復望者矣。

translations.literal: Now its empty name alone survives, and its discipline has still not revived; once it is crushed and suppressed, its authority will wither away, and nothing can be hoped for again.
translations.idiomatic: Now its empty name alone survives, and its discipline has still not revived; once it is crushed and suppressed, its authority will wither away, and nothing can be hoped for again.

sentences.zh: 昔阿合馬用事時，商賈賤役，皆行賄入官，及事敗，欲盡去其人，廷議以為不可，使阿合馬售私恩，而朝廷驟斂怨也。

translations.literal: Formerly when Ahmad held power, merchants and menial servants all gained office through bribery. When the affair collapsed, some wished to remove all such men entirely, but court deliberation held this impossible, lest Ahmad be allowed to dispense private favors while the court suddenly gathered resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when Ahmad held power, merchants and menial servants all gained office through bribery. When the affair collapsed, some wished to remove all such men entirely, but court deliberation held this impossible, lest Ahmad be allowed to dispense private favors while the court suddenly gathered resentment.

sentences.zh: 乃使按察司劾去其不可者，然後吏有所憚，民有所赴訴。

translations.literal: They therefore had the surveillance commissions impeach and remove those who were unfit; only then did officials feel restraint, and the people had somewhere to bring complaints.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore had the surveillance commissions impeach and remove those who were unfit; only then did officials feel restraint, and the people had somewhere to bring complaints.

sentences.zh: 則是按察司者，國家當飭勵之，不可摧抑也。

translations.literal: The surveillance commissions, then, are what the state ought to encourage and strengthen — they must not be crushed and suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: The surveillance commissions, then, are what the state ought to encourage and strengthen — they must not be crushed and suppressed.

sentences.zh: 」悉從文用議。

translations.literal: " All fully followed Wenyong's argument.
translations.idiomatic: " All fully followed Wenyong's argument.

sentences.zh: 轉禮部尚書，遷翰林、集賢二院學士，知祕書監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of the Ministry of Rites, promoted to academician of the Hanlin and Jixian Academies, and made director of the Directorate of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of the Ministry of Rites, promoted to academician of the Hanlin and Jixian Academies, and made director of the Directorate of the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 時中書右丞盧世榮，以貨利得幸權要為貴官，陰結貪刻之黨，以錙銖掊克為功，乃建議曰：「我立法治財，視常歲當倍增，而民不擾也。

translations.literal: At that time Lu Shirong, right vice director of the Secretariat, had gained favor with the powerful through profit and become a high official; he secretly joined a faction of the greedy and harsh, taking penny-by-penny extortion as his achievement, and proposed: "If I establish laws to manage revenue, revenue should roughly double compared with an ordinary year, yet the people will not be disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lu Shirong, right vice director of the Secretariat, had gained favor with the powerful through profit and become a high official; he secretly joined a faction of the greedy and harsh, taking penny-by-penny extortion as his achievement, and proposed, "If I establish laws to manage revenue, revenue should roughly double compared with an ordinary year, yet the people will not be disturbed.

sentences.zh: 」詔下會議，人無敢言者。

translations.literal: " An edict was issued convening discussion, and no one dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict was issued convening discussion, and no one dared speak.

sentences.zh: 文用陽問曰：「此錢取於右丞之家耶？

translations.literal: Wenyong asked openly: "Is this money to be taken from the Vice Director's own household?
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong asked openly, "Is this money to be taken from the Vice Director's own household?

sentences.zh: 將取之於民耶？

translations.literal: Or is it to be taken from the people?
translations.idiomatic: Or is it to be taken from the people?

sentences.zh: 取於右丞之家，則不敢知；

translations.literal: If it is taken from the Vice Director's household, I dare not inquire further;
translations.idiomatic: If it is taken from the Vice Director's household, I dare not inquire further;

sentences.zh: 若取諸民，則有說矣。

translations.literal: but if it is taken from the people, then I have something to say.
translations.idiomatic: but if it is taken from the people, then I have something to say.

sentences.zh: 牧羊者，歲嘗兩剪其毛，今牧人日剪其毛而獻之，則主者固悅其得毛之多矣，然而羊無以避寒熱，即死且盡，毛又可得哉！

translations.literal: A shepherd ordinarily shears his flock twice a year; if the herdsman now shears their wool daily and presents it, the master will indeed be pleased at how much wool he receives — yet the sheep have no way to endure cold and heat, and will soon die to the last; how then can wool be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: A shepherd ordinarily shears his flock twice a year; if the herdsman now shears their wool daily and presents it, the master will indeed be pleased at how much wool he receives — yet the sheep have no way to endure cold and heat, and will soon die to the last; how then can wool be obtained!

sentences.zh: 民財亦有限，取之以時，猶懼其傷殘也。

translations.literal: The people's wealth, too, has its limits; even when taken at the proper season, one still fears harming and crippling them.
translations.idiomatic: The people's wealth, too, has its limits; even when taken at the proper season, one still fears harming and crippling them.

sentences.zh: 今盡刻剝無遺，猶有百姓乎！

translations.literal: Now you would strip and peel them entirely without remainder — will there still be any common people!
translations.idiomatic: Now you would strip and peel them entirely without remainder — will there still be any common people!

sentences.zh: 」世榮不能對。

translations.literal: " Lu Shirong could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Shirong could not reply.

sentences.zh: 丞相安童謂坐中曰：「董尚書真不虛食俸祿者。

translations.literal: Chancellor Antong said to those seated: "Minister Dong truly does not eat his salary for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Antong said to those seated, "Minister Dong truly does not eat his salary for nothing.

sentences.zh: 」議者出，皆謝文用曰：「君以一言，折聚斂之臣，而厚邦本，真仁人之言哉。

translations.literal: " When the deliberators came out, all thanked Wenyong, saying: "With a single remark you have rebuffed a minister of exaction and strengthened the foundation of the state — truly the words of a benevolent man.
translations.idiomatic: " When the deliberators came out, all thanked Wenyong, saying, "With a single remark you have rebuffed a minister of exaction and strengthened the foundation of the state — truly the words of a benevolent man.

sentences.zh: 」世榮竟以是得罪。

translations.literal: " Lu Shirong ultimately fell from grace on this account.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Shirong ultimately fell from grace on this account.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，拜江淮行中書省參知政事，文用力辭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed vice director of the Jianghuai Branch Secretariat; Wenyong firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was appointed vice director of the Jianghuai Branch Secretariat; Wenyong firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿家世非他人比。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your family's standing is not comparable to others'.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your family's standing is not comparable to others'.

sentences.zh: 朕所以任卿者，不在錢穀細務也，卿當察其大者，事有不便，但言之。

translations.literal: The reason I appoint you is not for the petty affairs of revenue and grain; you should discern the larger matters, and whenever something is impracticable, simply speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I appoint you is not for the petty affairs of revenue and grain; you should discern the larger matters, and whenever something is impracticable, simply speak of it.

sentences.zh: 」文用遂行。

translations.literal: " Wenyong thereupon took up the post.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenyong thereupon took up the post.

sentences.zh: 行省長官者，素貴多傲，同列莫敢仰視，跪起稟白，如小吏事上官。

translations.literal: The chief directors of branch secretariats were by nature high in rank and often arrogant; their colleagues did not dare look up at them, kneeling and rising to report as petty clerks serving a superior.
translations.idiomatic: The chief directors of branch secretariats were by nature high in rank and often arrogant; their colleagues did not dare look up at them, kneeling and rising to report as petty clerks serving a superior.

sentences.zh: 文用至，則坐堂上，侃侃與論是非可否，無所遷就，雖數忤之，不顧也。

translations.literal: When Wenyong arrived, he sat in the hall and discussed right and wrong, feasibility and infeasibility, with easy forthrightness, yielding in nothing; though he repeatedly offended them, he paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyong arrived, he sat in the hall and discussed right and wrong, feasibility and infeasibility, with easy forthrightness, yielding in nothing; though he repeatedly offended them, he paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 有以帝命建佛塔於宋故宮者，有司奉行甚急，天大雨雪，入山伐木，死者數百人，猶欲併建大寺。

translations.literal: Someone, citing an imperial command, was building a Buddhist pagoda in the former Song palace; the relevant offices carried it out with great urgency. Heaven sent heavy rain and snow; men entered the mountains to fell timber, and several hundred died — yet they still wished to build a great monastery as well.
translations.idiomatic: Someone, citing an imperial command, was building a Buddhist pagoda in the former Song palace; the relevant offices carried it out with great urgency. Heaven sent heavy rain and snow; men entered the mountains to fell timber, and several hundred died — yet they still wished to build a great monastery as well.

sentences.zh: 文用謂其人曰：「非時役民，民不堪矣，少徐之如何？

translations.literal: Wenyong said to the man: "To impress the people at the wrong season — they cannot bear it. How about slowing the work a little?
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong said to the man, "To impress the people at the wrong season — they cannot bear it. How about slowing the work a little?

sentences.zh: 」長官者曰：「參政奈何格上命耶？

translations.literal: " The chief director said: "Vice Director, how can you obstruct an imperial command?
translations.idiomatic: " The chief director said, "Vice Director, how can you obstruct an imperial command?

sentences.zh: 」文用曰：「非敢格上命，今日之困民力而失民心者，豈上意耶！

translations.literal: " Wenyong said: "I do not dare obstruct the imperial command, but to exhaust the people's labor and lose the people's hearts today — can that be the emperor's intent!
translations.idiomatic: " Wenyong said, "I do not dare obstruct the imperial command, but to exhaust the people's labor and lose the people's hearts today — can that be the emperor's intent!

sentences.zh: 」其人意沮，遂稍寬其期。

translations.literal: " The man's spirit flagged, and he thereupon slightly extended the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: " The man's spirit flagged, and he thereupon slightly extended the deadline.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，朝廷將用兵海東，徵斂益急，有司大為奸利。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the court was about to use troops in the eastern sea; levies grew ever more urgent, and the relevant offices greatly profited through corruption.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year the court was about to use troops in the eastern sea; levies grew ever more urgent, and the relevant offices greatly profited through corruption.

sentences.zh: 文用請入奏事，大略言：「疲國家可寶之民力，取僻陋無用之小邦。

translations.literal: Wenyong requested permission to enter court and report; in outline he said: "To exhaust the state's precious people's strength in order to take a remote, useless little kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong requested permission to enter court and report; in outline he said, "To exhaust the state's precious people's strength in order to take a remote, useless little kingdom.

sentences.zh: 」列其條目甚悉。

translations.literal: " He listed the particulars in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: " He listed the particulars in great detail.

sentences.zh: 言上，事遂罷。

translations.literal: When he reported to the throne, the matter was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: When he reported to the throne, the matter was thereupon dropped.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 文用曰：「中丞不當理細務，吾當先舉賢才。

translations.literal: Wenyong said: "The censor-in-chief ought not to manage petty affairs; I should first recommend men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong said, "The censor-in-chief ought not to manage petty affairs; I should first recommend men of talent.

sentences.zh: 」乃舉胡祗遹、王惲、雷膺、荊幼紀、許楫、孔從道十餘人為按察使，徐琰、魏初為行臺中丞，當時以為極選。

translations.literal: " He then recommended more than ten men — Hu Zhiyuan, Wang Yun, Lei Ying, Jing Youji, Xu Ji, Kong Congdao, and others — as surveillance commissioners, and Xu Yan and Wei Chu as censors-in-chief of the Branch Secretariat; at the time these were considered the finest selections.
translations.idiomatic: " He then recommended more than ten men — Hu Zhiyuan, Wang Yun, Lei Ying, Jing Youji, Xu Ji, Kong Congdao, and others — as surveillance commissioners, and Xu Yan and Wei Chu as censors-in-chief of the Branch Secretariat; at the time these were considered the finest selections.

sentences.zh: 方是時，桑哥當國，恩寵方盛，自近戚貴人見之，皆屏息遜避，無敢誰何。

translations.literal: At that time Sangha held the state; favor and power were at their height. Even close kin and nobles, on seeing him, all held their breath and yielded, not daring to challenge him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sangha held the state; favor and power were at their height. Even close kin and nobles, on seeing him, all held their breath and yielded, not daring to challenge him.

sentences.zh: 文用以舊臣任中丞，獨不附之。

translations.literal: Wenyong, as a former minister serving as censor-in-chief, alone would not attach himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong, as a former minister serving as censor-in-chief, alone would not attach himself to him.

sentences.zh: 桑哥令人風文用頌己功於帝前，文用不荅。

translations.literal: Sangha had someone hint to Wenyong that he should praise Sangha's achievements before the emperor; Wenyong did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Sangha had someone hint to Wenyong that he should praise Sangha's achievements before the emperor; Wenyong did not respond.

sentences.zh: 桑哥又自謂文用曰：「百司皆具食於丞相府矣。

translations.literal: Sangha also said to Wenyong himself: "All the hundred offices already take their meals at the chancellor's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Sangha also said to Wenyong himself, "All the hundred offices already take their meals at the chancellor's residence.

sentences.zh: 」文用又不荅。

translations.literal: " Wenyong again did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenyong again did not respond.

sentences.zh: 會朔方軍興，糧糗粗備，而誅求愈急，文用謂桑哥曰：「民急矣。

translations.literal: It happened that military operations arose in Shuofang; grain and provisions were roughly in place, yet exactions grew ever more urgent. Wenyong said to Sangha: "The people are in distress.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that military operations arose in Shuofang; grain and provisions were roughly in place, yet exactions grew ever more urgent. Wenyong said to Sangha, "The people are in distress.

sentences.zh: 外難未解而內伐其根本，丞相宜思之。

translations.literal: External danger is not yet resolved, yet you ravage the foundations within — Chancellor, you ought to consider this.
translations.idiomatic: External danger is not yet resolved, yet you ravage the foundations within — Chancellor, you ought to consider this.

sentences.zh: 」於是遠邇盜賊蜂起，文用持外郡所上盜賊之目，謂桑哥曰：「百姓豈不欲生養安樂哉！

translations.literal: " Thereupon bandits rose near and far like swarming bees. Wenyong took the registers of bandits submitted by outer commanderies and said to Sangha: "Do the common people not wish to live, be nourished, and dwell in peace!
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon bandits rose near and far like swarming bees. Wenyong took the registers of bandits submitted by outer commanderies and said to Sangha, "Do the common people not wish to live, be nourished, and dwell in peace!

sentences.zh: 急法暴斂使至此爾。

translations.literal: Harsh laws and violent exactions have brought them to this.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh laws and violent exactions have brought them to this.

sentences.zh: 御史臺所以救政事之不及，丞相當助之，不當抑之也。

translations.literal: The Censorate exists to remedy what government cannot reach in time; the Chancellor ought to assist it, not suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate exists to remedy what government cannot reach in time; the Chancellor ought to assist it, not suppress it.

sentences.zh: 御史臺不得行，則民無所赴愬；

translations.literal: If the Censorate cannot act, the people have nowhere to bring grievances;
translations.idiomatic: If the Censorate cannot act, the people have nowhere to bring grievances;

sentences.zh: 民無所赴愬，而政日亂，將不止於臺事之不行也。

translations.literal: when the people have nowhere to bring grievances, government grows daily more chaotic — and the harm will not stop at the Censorate's inability to act.
translations.idiomatic: when the people have nowhere to bring grievances, government grows daily more chaotic — and the harm will not stop at the Censorate's inability to act.

sentences.zh: 」忤其意益深，乃摭拾臺事百端，文用日與辨論，不為屈。

translations.literal: " He offended Sangha's intent ever more deeply; Sangha then collected a hundred pretexts from Censorate affairs, and Wenyong debated with him day after day without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: " He offended Sangha's intent ever more deeply; Sangha then collected a hundred pretexts from Censorate affairs, and Wenyong debated with him day after day without yielding.

sentences.zh: 於是具奏桑哥姦狀，詔報文用，語密而外人不知也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he fully memorialized Sangha's corrupt conduct; an edict replied to Wenyong, the words secret so that outsiders did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he fully memorialized Sangha's corrupt conduct; an edict replied to Wenyong, the words secret so that outsiders did not know.

sentences.zh: 桑哥日誣譖文用于帝曰：「在朝惟董文用戇傲不聽令，沮撓尚書省，請痛治其罪。

translations.literal: Sangha daily slandered Wenyong to the emperor, saying: "In court only Dong Wenyong is obstinate and arrogant, disobeying orders and obstructing the Secretariat — I beg that his crime be severely punished.
translations.idiomatic: Sangha daily slandered Wenyong to the emperor, saying, "In court only Dong Wenyong is obstinate and arrogant, disobeying orders and obstructing the Secretariat — I beg that his crime be severely punished.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「彼御史之職也，何罪之有！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "That is the censor's duty — what crime is there!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "That is the censor's duty — what crime is there!

sentences.zh: 且董文用端謹，朕所素知，汝善視之。

translations.literal: Moreover Dong Wenyong is upright and careful — I have long known this. Treat him well.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Dong Wenyong is upright and careful — I have long known this. Treat him well.

sentences.zh: 」遷大司農。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Grand Director of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to Grand Director of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 時欲奪民田為屯田，文用固執不可。

translations.literal: At that time there was a plan to seize the people's fields for military colonies; Wenyong firmly held that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was a plan to seize the people's fields for military colonies; Wenyong firmly held that this could not be done.

sentences.zh: 遷為翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be chief academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to be chief academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，隆福太后在東宮，以文用舊臣，欲使文用授皇孫經，具奏上，以帝命命之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Empress Dowager Longfu was in the Eastern Palace. As Wenyong was an old minister, she wished to have Wenyong instruct the imperial grandson in the classics; she fully memorialized the throne, and by the emperor's command he was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, Longfu Empress Dowager resided in the Eastern Palace. Knowing Wenyong to be a veteran of the old court, she wanted him to teach the classics to the imperial grandson; she submitted a full memorial, and the emperor ordered it done.

sentences.zh: 文用每講說經旨，必附以朝廷故事，丁嚀譬喻，反復開悟，皇孫亦特加敬禮。

translations.literal: Whenever Wenyong lectured on the meaning of the classics, he always appended court precedents, earnestly illustrating with analogies and repeatedly opening understanding; the imperial grandson likewise showed him special respect and courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Wenyong expounded the classics, he wove in stories from court history, urging and illustrating his points until the lesson took hold; the imperial grandson treated him with marked deference.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，帝命文用以其諸子入見，文用曰：「臣蒙國厚恩，死無以報，臣之子，何能為！

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year the emperor ordered Wenyong to bring his sons for an audience. Wenyong said: "Your subject has received the state's deep grace; in death I have no way to repay it — what could my sons do!
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year the emperor ordered Wenyong to present his sons at court. Wenyong replied, "I owe the state a debt I cannot repay even with my life — what could my sons possibly offer!

sentences.zh: 」命至再三，終不以見。

translations.literal: " The order came again and again, yet in the end he would not have them presented.
translations.idiomatic: " The command was repeated several times, but he never brought them forward.

sentences.zh: 是歲，世祖崩，成宗將即位上都，太后命文用從行。

translations.literal: That year Kublai passed away. Temür was about to accede at Shangdu; the empress dowager ordered Wenyong to accompany the journey.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Kublai died. As Temür prepared to take the throne at Shangdu, the empress dowager told Wenyong to travel with the party.

sentences.zh: 既即位，巡狩三不剌之地，文用曰：「先帝新棄天下，陛下巡狩，不以時還，無以慰安元元，宜趣還京師。

translations.literal: Once he had acceded, he went on an imperial hunt to the land of Sanbula. Wenyong said: "The late emperor has newly abandoned All-under-Heaven; Your Majesty hunts abroad and does not return in season — there is no way to comfort and reassure the myriad people. You ought to hurry back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After his accession Temür went hunting in Sanbula. Wenyong remonstrated, "The late emperor has only just departed; if Your Majesty hunts far from the capital and does not return in good time, you cannot reassure the common people. You should return to the capital at once.

sentences.zh: 且臣聞人君猶北辰然，居其所而衆星拱之，不在勤遠略也。

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard that the ruler is like the Pole Star: remaining in his place, the myriad stars incline toward him — it does not lie in being diligent at distant campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I have heard that a ruler is like the North Star — he stays fixed in place while the other stars wheel around him. His task is not to exhaust himself on distant expeditions.

sentences.zh: 」帝悟，即日可其奏。

translations.literal: " The emperor understood and that same day approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took his point and approved the memorial that very day.
