sentences.zh: 是行也，帝每召入帳中，問先朝故事，文用亦盛言先帝虛心納賢、開國經世之務，談說或至夜半。

translations.literal: On this journey the emperor frequently summoned him into the tent to ask about precedents of the former reign; Wenyong also spoke at length of the late emperor's open-hearted acceptance of the worthy and the tasks of founding the state and governing the age — their discussions sometimes lasted until midnight.
translations.idiomatic: During the journey Temür often called Wenyong into his tent to ask about precedents from Kublai's reign. Wenyong spoke at length of how the late emperor had welcomed talent and built the institutions of the new dynasty; their talks sometimes ran until midnight.

sentences.zh: 文用自先帝時，每侍燕，與蒙古大臣同列，裕宗嘗就榻上賜酒，使毋下拜跪飲，皆異數也。

translations.literal: From Kublai's time onward, whenever Wenyong attended banquets he sat in the same rank as Mongol ministers; Crown Prince Zhenjin (Yuzong) once granted him wine from the couch, instructing him not to descend, bow, and kneel to drink — all extraordinary honors.
translations.idiomatic: Since Kublai's day Wenyong had sat at banquets in the same rank as Mongol ministers — a rare privilege. Crown Prince Zhenjin (Yuzong) once offered him wine from his couch and told him not to kneel and bow to drink; such honors were granted to few.

sentences.zh: 帝在東宮時，正旦受賀，於衆中見文用，召使前曰：「吾向見至尊，甚稱汝賢。

translations.literal: When the emperor was in the Eastern Palace, at New Year's he received congratulations; spotting Wenyong among the crowd, he summoned him forward and said: "When I recently saw the Supreme One, he greatly praised your worth.
translations.idiomatic: While Temür was still crown prince, at New Year's he received congratulations. Seeing Wenyong in the crowd, he called him forward and said, "When I last saw the emperor, he spoke very highly of your talents.

sentences.zh: 」輒親取酒飲之。

translations.literal: " He then personally took wine and had him drink it.
translations.idiomatic: " He then poured wine himself and had Wenyong drink it.

sentences.zh: 至是，眷賚益厚。

translations.literal: By now favor and bestowal grew ever richer.
translations.idiomatic: From then on imperial favor and gifts grew ever more generous.

sentences.zh: 是年，詔修先帝實錄，陞資德大夫、知制誥兼修國史。

translations.literal: That year an edict ordered the compilation of the Veritable Records of the late emperor; he was promoted to Grand Master of Brilliant Talent, controller of draft edicts, and concurrently compiler of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict commissioned the Veritable Records of Kublai. Wenyong was promoted to Grand Master of Brilliant Talent, put in charge of drafting edicts, and made a concurrent compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 文用於祖宗世系功德、近戚將相家世勳績，皆記憶貫穿，史館有所考究質問，文用應之無遺失。

translations.literal: Wenyong had the ancestral lines, merits, and achievements of the imperial house, and the family backgrounds and recorded exploits of close kin and generals and chancellors all committed to memory in continuous thread; whenever the historiographical office had inquiries to investigate and put to the test, Wenyong answered without omission.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong carried in his head the full genealogy and achievements of the imperial clan and the family histories and battle records of the great kin and ministers. Whenever the historiographical office needed to verify a detail, he answered completely and without error.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，上章請老，賜中統鈔萬貫以歸，官一子，鄉郡侍養。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; he was granted ten thousand strings of Zhongtong paper money to return home, one son was given office, and he was to be tended in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dade he petitioned to retire. The court granted him ten thousand strings of Zhongtong paper money for his journey home, gave one son an official post, and allowed him to be cared for in his native district.

sentences.zh: 六月戊寅，以疾卒，年七十有四。

translations.literal: On wuyin of the sixth month he died of illness, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day of the sixth month he died of illness at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 子八人：士貞，士亨，士楷，士英，士昌，士恒，士廉，士方。

translations.literal: He had eight sons: Shizhen, Shiheng, Shikai, Shiying, Shichang, Shi Heng, Shilian, and Shifang.
translations.idiomatic: He left eight sons: Shizhen, Shiheng, Shikai, Shiying, Shichang, Shi Heng, Shilian, and Shifang.

sentences.zh: 贈銀青榮祿大夫、少保、趙國公，諡忠穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Silver-Girdled Grand Master for Glorious Blessings, Junior Guardian, and Duke of Zhao; his posthumous title was Zhongmu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Silver-Girdled Grand Master for Glorious Blessings, Junior Guardian, and Duke of Zhao, with the posthumous name Loyal and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 文直字彥正，俊之第四子也。

translations.literal: Wenzhi, styled Yan Zheng, was Jun's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhi, courtesy name Yan Zheng, was the fourth son of Jun.

sentences.zh: 剛毅莊栗，簡言笑，通經史法律。

translations.literal: He was resolute and sternly dignified, sparing in speech and laughter, and versed in the classics, histories, and law.
translations.idiomatic: Steadfast and grave in bearing, he spoke little and laughed less, and was thoroughly versed in the classics, histories, and law.

sentences.zh: 為藁城長官，佩金符。

translations.literal: He served as chief magistrate of Gaocheng, wearing a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief magistrate of Gaocheng and carried a gold tally of authority.

sentences.zh: 初，兄文炳及季弟文忠，去事世祖，次文用亦在朝，俱有仰於家，而食者餘百口，文直勤儉，始終不替。

translations.literal: Initially his elder brother Wenbing and youngest brother Wenzhong left to serve Kublai; next Wenyong was also at court — all depended on the household for support, while more than a hundred mouths ate there. Wenzhi was diligent and frugal throughout without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: At first his elder brother Wenbing and youngest brother Wenzhong went off to serve Kublai, and Wenyong soon followed them to court. The family depended on those salaries, yet more than a hundred mouths still had to be fed at home. Wenzhi kept the household through thrift and hard work, never letting standards slip.

sentences.zh: 內則養生送死之合禮，外則中表賓問之中度，奉上接下，一敬一愛，藹乎其睦也。

translations.literal: Within the household he saw to nourishing the living and burying the dead according to ritual propriety; without, he observed proper measure in relations with kin and guests; in serving superiors and receiving subordinates, each act carried reverence and affection — harmonious indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Within the family he saw that the living were cared for and the dead buried according to ritual; with kin and guests he kept relations warm but measured. Whether serving superiors or dealing with inferiors, he showed equal respect and kindness — the household lived in genuine harmony.

sentences.zh: 性好施而甚仁，里閈或貧不自立，每陰濟其急，不使之知恩所從來。

translations.literal: By nature he loved giving and was deeply humane; when neighbors in the lanes were poor and could not support themselves, he often secretly relieved their distress, never letting them know whence the kindness came.
translations.idiomatic: Generous and deeply humane by nature, he would quietly aid neighbors who could not support themselves, never letting them discover who had helped them.

sentences.zh: 微至僮病，必手予粥藥。

translations.literal: Even down to a servant boy's illness, he would personally hand over gruel and medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Even when a household servant fell ill, he would personally bring gruel and medicine.

sentences.zh: 或止之，曰：「不忍以其賤違吾愛心。

translations.literal: When some tried to stop him, he said: "I cannot bear to let their low station violate my loving heart.
translations.idiomatic: When others tried to dissuade him, he said, "I cannot let their humble rank keep me from doing what love requires.

sentences.zh: 」及棄官，浮沉里社，任真適意，親賓過從，尊酒相勞。

translations.literal: " After leaving office he drifted within the village community, following his true inclinations as he saw fit; when kin and guests came and went, they shared honored wine and mutual comfort.
translations.idiomatic: " After he left office he lived quietly among his neighbors, doing as he pleased. When friends and kin visited, they shared wine and easy conversation.

sentences.zh: 家門日以烜赫，己獨恬然，不見諸辭色。

translations.literal: As the family gate grew daily more brilliant and renowned, he alone remained placid, showing nothing of it in word or expression.
translations.idiomatic: As the Dong family grew ever more illustrious, he alone remained serene, never betraying pride in word or manner.

sentences.zh: 以病卒，年五十有二。

translations.literal: He died of illness, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 文忠字彥誠，俊第八子也。

translations.literal: Wenzhong, styled Yan Cheng, was Jun's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong, courtesy name Yan Cheng, was Jun's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 歲壬子，入侍世祖潛邸。

translations.literal: In the year renzi he entered service at Kublai's private residence while heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the renzi year he entered service at Kublai's household while the latter was still heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 王鶚嘗言詩，因問文忠能之乎，文忠曰：「吾少讀書，惟知入則孝於親，出則忠於君而已。

translations.literal: Wang He once spoke of poetry and thereupon asked whether Wenzhong could do it. Wenzhong said: "In youth when I read books, I knew only to be filial to parents at home and loyal to the ruler abroad — that alone.
translations.idiomatic: Wang He once spoke about poetry and asked whether Wenzhong could compose it. Wenzhong replied, "When I was young I studied only what every man should know: filial piety at home and loyalty to the ruler abroad.

sentences.zh: 詩非所學也。

translations.literal: Poetry is not what I studied.
translations.idiomatic: Poetry was never part of my training.

sentences.zh: 」癸丑，從征南詔。

translations.literal: " In guichou he followed the campaign against Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: " In guichou he accompanied the campaign against Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 己未，伐宋，與兄文炳、文用敗宋兵於陽羅堡，得蒙衝百艘，進圍鄂。

translations.literal: In jiwei, campaigning against Song, together with his elder brothers Wenbing and Wenyong he defeated Song troops at Yangluo Fort, seized a hundred masked assault ships, and advanced to besiege Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei, during the campaign against Song, he and his brothers Wenbing and Wenyong routed the Song army at Yangluo Fort, captured a hundred warships, and pressed on to besiege Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，侍講學士徒單公履欲奏行貢舉，知帝於釋氏重教而輕禪，乃言儒亦有之，科舉類教，道學類禪。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Lecturer-in-Attendance Tuotuo Gonglu wished to memorialize implementing the examination system for selecting officials. Knowing the emperor in Buddhism valued the Teaching and slighted Chan, he said Confucianism also had such distinctions: the examination system resembled the Teaching, the Learning of the Way resembled Chan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Tuotuo Gonglu, lecturer-in-attendance, planned to memorialize restoring the civil service examinations. Knowing that Kublai in Buddhist matters favored doctrinal teaching over Chan meditation, he argued that Confucianism had a parallel: examinations were like doctrinal teaching, while Neo-Confucian moral philosophy was like Chan.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，召姚樞、許衡與宰臣廷辨。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and summoned Yao Shu, Xu Heng, and the chief ministers for court debate.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai was angered and summoned Yao Shu, Xu Heng, and the chief ministers to debate the matter at court.

sentences.zh: 文忠自外入，帝曰：「汝日誦四書，亦道學者。

translations.literal: Wenzhong entered from outside. The emperor said: "You who daily recite the Four Books — you too are a practitioner of the Learning of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong came in from outside. The emperor said to him, "You recite the Four Books every day — you are a practitioner of the Learning of the Way yourself.

sentences.zh: 」文忠對曰：「陛下每言：士不治經講孔孟之道而為詩賦，何關修身，何益治國！

translations.literal: " Wenzhong replied: "Your Majesty has often said: When scholars do not study the classics and expound the Way of Confucius and Mencius but instead compose poetry and rhapsodies — what relation has that to self-cultivation, what benefit to governing the state!
translations.idiomatic: " Wenzhong answered, "Your Majesty has often said that when scholars neglect the classics and the teachings of Confucius and Mencius to write poetry and rhapsodies, what does that have to do with self-cultivation or governing the realm!

sentences.zh: 由是海內之士，稍知從事實學。

translations.literal: Because of this scholars throughout the realm gradually came to know they should pursue substantive learning.
translations.idiomatic: Since then scholars across the empire have gradually turned to practical learning.

sentences.zh: 臣今所誦，皆孔孟之言，焉知所謂道學！

translations.literal: What I now recite are all words of Confucius and Mencius — how would I know what is called the Learning of the Way!
translations.idiomatic: What I recite are the words of Confucius and Mencius — I know nothing of this so-called Learning of the Way!

sentences.zh: 而俗儒守亡國餘習，欲行其說，故以是上惑聖聽，恐非陛下教人修身治國之意也。

translations.literal: Yet vulgar Confucians cling to the surviving habits of a fallen state and wish to propagate their doctrine; therefore they use this to confuse Your Majesty's sacred hearing — I fear this is not Your Majesty's intent in teaching people self-cultivation and governing the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet pedantic scholars cling to the bad habits that helped destroy the previous dynasty and wish to push their own doctrine. They use this comparison to mislead Your Majesty — I fear that is not what you mean by teaching self-cultivation and good government.

sentences.zh: 」事遂止。

translations.literal: " The affair thereupon ceased.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十一年，伐宋，民困供饋，文忠奏免常歲橫征，從之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, campaigning against Song, the people were distressed by supplying provisions; Wenzhong memorialized exempting the annual arbitrary levies, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, as the war against Song continued, the people were worn down by supplying the army. Wenzhong memorialized to abolish the annual arbitrary levies, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗見宋降將，從容問宋所以亡者，皆曰：「賈似道當國，薄武人而重文儒，將士怨之，莫有鬪志。

translations.literal: The emperor once saw Song generals who had surrendered and casually asked why Song had perished; they all said: "Jia Sidao held the state — he slighted military men and valued literary Confucians; officers and soldiers resented him and none had fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai once received surrendered Song generals and casually asked why the Song had fallen. They all said, "Jia Sidao ran the government — he looked down on soldiers and favored literary men. The officers and troops resented him and had no will to fight.

sentences.zh: 故大軍既至，爭解甲歸命也。

translations.literal: Therefore when the great army arrived, all vied to cast off armor and submit.
translations.idiomatic: So when your great army arrived, we all cast off our armor and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 」帝問文忠：「此言何如？

translations.literal: " The emperor asked Wenzhong: "What do you think of these words?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor turned to Wenzhong and asked, "What do you make of that?

sentences.zh: 」文忠因詰之曰：「似道薄汝矣，而君則貴汝以官，富汝以祿，未嘗薄汝也。

translations.literal: " Wenzhong thereupon pressed them, saying: "Sidao slighted you — yet your sovereign honored you with office and enriched you with stipends; he never slighted you.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenzhong pressed them: "Sidao may have slighted you, but your emperor honored you with rank and enriched you with salary — he never slighted you at all.

sentences.zh: 今有怨於相，而移於君，不肯一戰，坐視國亡，如臣節何！

translations.literal: Now you bear resentment toward the chancellor and transfer it to your lord — you refuse a single battle and sit watching the state perish; what of the integrity owed a subject!
translations.idiomatic: Now you hold a grudge against the chancellor and take it out on your sovereign — you would not fight a single battle and sat by while the state fell. What kind of loyalty is that!

sentences.zh: 然則似道薄汝者，豈非預知汝曹不足恃乎！

translations.literal: In that case, when Sidao slighted you, was it not because he foresaw that you lot could not be relied upon!
translations.idiomatic: In that case, when Sidao slighted you, was it not because he already knew you could not be counted on!

sentences.zh: 」帝深善之。

translations.literal: " The emperor deeply approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 有旨徙大都獵戶於郢中，文忠奏止之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered relocating hunt households of the capital to Yingzhong; Wenzhong memorialized to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered moving the capital's hunting households to Yingzhong; Wenzhong memorialized against it and the order was halted.

sentences.zh: 又請罷官鬻田器之稅，聽民自為。

translations.literal: He also requested abolishing the government tax on selling farm implements, allowing the people to make their own.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the government monopoly tax on farm tools be abolished so that people could make and sell them freely.

sentences.zh: 時多盜，詔犯者皆殺無赦。

translations.literal: At that time theft was widespread; an edict declared all offenders would be killed without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Theft was rampant at the time, and an edict declared that all offenders would be executed without mercy.

sentences.zh: 在處繫囚滿獄。

translations.literal: Everywhere prisons were filled with detainees.
translations.idiomatic: Prisons everywhere overflowed with prisoners.

sentences.zh: 文忠言：「殺人取貨，與竊一錢者均死，慘黷莫甚，恐乖陛下好生之德。

translations.literal: Wenzhong said: "Killing for goods and stealing a single coin receiving equal death — nothing could be more cruel and profane; I fear this runs counter to Your Majesty's virtue of cherishing life.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong said, "To put a murderer who robs for profit and a thief who steals a single coin to the same death — nothing could be more cruel or unjust. I fear this violates Your Majesty's virtue of cherishing life.

sentences.zh: 」敕革之。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered this changed.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict was issued revising the policy.

sentences.zh: 或告漢人毆傷國人，及太府監屬盧甲盜剪官布。

translations.literal: Someone reported that a Han man had beaten and injured a Mongol subject, and that Lu Jia, an attendant of the Imperial Storehouse Directorate, had stolen and clipped official cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that a Han man had beaten a Mongol subject, and that Lu Jia, an attendant of the Imperial Storehouse Directorate, had stolen and cut official cloth.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命殺以懲衆。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and ordered them killed to warn the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered both men executed as a warning to others.

sentences.zh: 文忠言：「今刑曹於囚罪當死者，已有服辭，猶必詳讞，是豈可因人一言，遽加之重典！

translations.literal: Wenzhong said: "Now even when the penal office has a prisoner whose crime merits death and who has already confessed, they still must thoroughly review the case — how then can one hastily impose the heavy penalty on the basis of a single person's word!
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong said, "Even when the penal office has a prisoner who has confessed to a capital crime, the case must still be carefully reviewed. How can we impose the death penalty on the strength of a single accusation!

sentences.zh: 宜付有司閱實，以俟後命。

translations.literal: They ought to be handed to the proper offices to verify the facts, awaiting further command.
translations.idiomatic: They should be handed to the proper offices for investigation, and sentence should await your further command.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣文忠及近臣突滿分覈之，皆得其誣狀，遂詔原之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Wenzhong and a close minister Tumang were dispatched to investigate separately; in every case they found false accusations, and an edict pardoned the accused.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenzhong and a close minister named Tumang were sent to investigate separately. Both cases proved to be false accusations, and an edict pardoned the accused.

sentences.zh: 帝因責侍臣曰：「方朕怒時，卿曹皆不敢言。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon rebuked the attendants, saying: "When I was angry, you all dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then rebuked his attendants, saying, "When I was angry, none of you dared speak up.

sentences.zh: 非董文忠開悟朕心，則殺二無辜之人，必取議中外矣。

translations.literal: Had not Dong Wenzhong opened and awakened my mind, I would have killed two innocent men — and would surely have drawn criticism within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Had Dong Wenzhong not set me straight, I would have killed two innocent men and brought reproach on the court at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 」因賜文忠金尊，曰：「用旌卿直。

translations.literal: " He then granted Wenzhong a gold goblet, saying: "This is to honor your directness.
translations.idiomatic: " He then presented Wenzhong with a gold goblet, saying, "This is to honor your forthrightness.

sentences.zh: 」裕宗亦語宮臣曰：「方天威之震，董文忠從容諫正，實人臣難能者。

translations.literal: " Crown Prince Zhenjin (Yuzong) also told palace officials: "When imperial wrath was shaken, Dong Wenzhong calmly remonstrated and set matters right — truly something difficult for a subject to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: " Crown Prince Zhenjin (Yuzong) also told palace officials, "When the emperor's wrath was at its height, Dong Wenzhong calmly remonstrated with him — that is something few subjects could manage.

sentences.zh: 」太府監屬奉物詣文忠泣謝曰：「鄙人賴公復生。

translations.literal: " An attendant of the Imperial Storehouse Directorate brought gifts to Wenzhong and tearfully thanked him, saying: "This lowly man owes his renewed life to you, sir.
translations.idiomatic: " The Imperial Storehouse attendant brought gifts to Wenzhong and wept as he thanked him, saying, "I owe my life to you, sir.

sentences.zh: 」文忠曰：「吾素非知子，所以相救於危急者，蓋為國平刑，豈望子見報哉！

translations.literal: " Wenzhong said: "I have never known you — the reason I rescued you in your extremity was simply to settle punishments fairly for the state; how could I expect repayment from you!
translations.idiomatic: " Wenzhong said, "I barely know you. I helped you in your extremity only because the state must administer justice fairly — I never expected any reward from you!

sentences.zh: 」却其物不受。

translations.literal: " He refused the gifts and would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused the gifts.

sentences.zh: 自安童北伐，阿合馬獨當國柄，大立親黨，懼廉希憲復入為相，害其私計，奏希憲以右丞行省江陵。

translations.literal: Since Antong's northern campaign, Ahmad alone held the reins of state, greatly establishing his own faction; fearing Lian Xixian might return as chancellor and harm his private designs, he memorialized that Xixian be sent as right vice director to govern Jiangling Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Antong marched north, Ahmad alone controlled the government and packed offices with his allies. Fearing that Lian Xixian might return as chancellor and upset his plans, he had Xixian posted as right vice director to govern Jiangling Province.

sentences.zh: 文忠言：「希憲，國家名臣。

translations.literal: Wenzhong said: "Xixian is a renowned minister of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong said, "Xixian is one of the state's most distinguished ministers.

sentences.zh: 今宰相虛位，不可使久居外，以孤人望，宜早召還。

translations.literal: Now the chancellorship stands vacant — he must not be kept abroad long, lest public expectation be isolated; he should be recalled early.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellorship is now vacant. He should not be kept away from court so long that public confidence is lost. He ought to be recalled at once.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十六年十月，奏曰：「陛下始以燕王為中書令、樞密使，纔一至中書。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixteenth year he memorialized, saying: "Your Majesty initially appointed the Prince of Yan as director of the Secretariat and commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs — he had scarcely reached the Secretariat once.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the sixteenth year he memorialized, saying, "Your Majesty first appointed the Prince of Yan director of the Secretariat and commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, yet he barely set foot in the Secretariat once.

sentences.zh: 自冊為太子，累使明習軍國之事，然十有餘年，終守謙退，不肯視事者，非不奉明詔也，蓋朝廷處之未盡其道爾。

translations.literal: Since he was enfeoffed as crown prince, Your Majesty repeatedly had him clearly familiarize himself with military and state affairs; yet for more than ten years he has consistently kept to modesty and declined, refusing to manage affairs — this is not failing to obey clear edicts; rather the court has not fully disposed matters according to the proper Way.
translations.idiomatic: Since he was made crown prince, Your Majesty has repeatedly instructed him in military and state affairs. Yet for more than ten years he has remained modest and refused to take charge — not because he disobeys your edicts, but because the court has not arranged matters in a way that allows him to do so properly.

sentences.zh: 夫事已奏決，而始啟太子，是使臣子而可否君父之命，故惟有唯默避遜而已。

translations.literal: For once matters have already been memorialized and decided, the crown prince is only then informed — this makes subjects approve or reject the lord-father's commands; hence he can only remain silent and yield.
translations.idiomatic: When matters are already decided before the crown prince is consulted, he is placed in the position of approving or rejecting his father's orders. That is why he can only keep silent and hold back.

sentences.zh: 以臣所知，不若令有司先啟而後聞，其有未安者，則以詔敕斷之，庶幾理順而分不踰，太子必不敢辭其責矣。

translations.literal: As I understand it, it would be better to have the responsible offices report first and the crown prince hear afterward; where anything is unsatisfactory, let an edict decide — then principle will be orderly and roles will not be overstepped, and the crown prince will not dare shirk his responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: In my view, the responsible offices should report to the crown prince first and then submit to Your Majesty. Where anything is unsatisfactory, let an edict settle it. Then roles will be clear, boundaries respected, and the crown prince will not dare evade his duties.

sentences.zh: 」帝即日召大臣，面諭其意，使行之。

translations.literal: " The emperor that same day summoned the chief ministers, personally instructed them in his intent, and had it carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day the emperor summoned the chief ministers, explained his intent in person, and ordered the new procedure implemented.

sentences.zh: 復語太子曰：「董八，崇立國本者，其勿忘之。」

translations.literal: He also told the crown prince: "Dong Eight — he who exalted the foundation of the state; do not forget this."
translations.idiomatic: He also told the crown prince, "Dong Eight — the man who strengthened the foundation of the realm. Do not forget him."

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書謝昌元請立門下省，封駁制敕，以絕中書風曉近習奏請之弊。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Xie Changyuan requested establishing a Gate Department to seal and return imperial edicts, cutting off the Secretariat's practice of favoring close attendants in memorializing requests.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Changyuan, minister of rites, proposed establishing a Gate Department with power to seal and return edicts, to end the Secretariat's habit of pushing petitions through favored court insiders.

sentences.zh: 帝銳意欲行之，詔廷臣雜議；

translations.literal: The emperor was keen to implement it and ordered court ministers to discuss it jointly;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was eager to put the plan into effect and ordered the court ministers to debate it;

sentences.zh: 且怒翰林學士承旨王磐曰：「如是有益之事，汝不入告，而使南方後至之臣言之，汝用學問何為！

translations.literal: and also angrily told Chief Hanlin Academician Wang Pan: "On a matter so beneficial as this, you did not report it to me and instead let a southern minister who arrived later speak of it — of what use is your learning!
translations.idiomatic: He also angrily rebuked Chief Hanlin Academician Wang Pan, saying, "On a proposal this valuable, you never brought it to my attention, yet you let a southern official who arrived later speak of it first — what good is all your learning!

sentences.zh: 必今日開是省。

translations.literal: It must be opened today.
translations.idiomatic: This department must be established today.

sentences.zh: 」三日，廷臣奏以文忠為侍中，及其屬數十人。

translations.literal: " Three days later court ministers memorialized appointing Wenzhong as palace attendant, along with several dozen subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: " Three days later the court ministers memorialized appointing Wenzhong as palace attendant, together with several dozen subordinates.

sentences.zh: 近臣乘便言曰：「陛下將別置省，此實其時。

translations.literal: A close minister seized the opportunity to say: "Your Majesty wishes to establish a separate department — this is truly the time.
translations.idiomatic: A close minister seized the moment to say, "Your Majesty plans to set up a separate department — now is the time.

sentences.zh: 然得人則可以寬聖心，新民聽；

translations.literal: Yet if the right men are obtained, the sacred mind can be eased and the people's hearing renewed;
translations.idiomatic: But with the right men in place, Your Majesty's mind can be at ease and the people reassured;

sentences.zh: 今聞盜詐之臣與居其間，不可。

translations.literal: now I hear that thieving, deceitful ministers would sit among them — this will not do.
translations.idiomatic: yet I hear that thieving, deceitful ministers would serve among them — that will not do.

sentences.zh: 」其言多指文忠。

translations.literal: " His words largely pointed at Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: " His remarks were largely aimed at Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 文忠忿辨曰：「上每稱臣不盜不詐，今汝顧臣而言，意實在臣。

translations.literal: Wenzhong angrily argued back: "The sovereign has often called me neither thieving nor deceitful; now you look toward me as you speak — your intent is truly directed at me.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong angrily retorted, "The emperor has often praised me as honest and trustworthy. You look straight at me as you speak — you clearly mean me.

sentences.zh: 其顯言臣盜詐何事！

translations.literal: State clearly what thieving or deceit you accuse me of!
translations.idiomatic: Name plainly what thieving or deceit you accuse me of!

sentences.zh: 」帝令言者出，文忠猶訴不止，且攻其害國之姦。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered the speaker out; Wenzhong still pressed his grievance without stopping, and also attacked him as a traitor harmful to the state.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor had the accuser removed, but Wenzhong continued protesting and denounced him as a traitor who harmed the state.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕自知之，彼不言汝也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I know this myself — he was not speaking of you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I know what happened — he was not referring to you.

sentences.zh: 」其人忌文忠，欲中害之，然以文忠清慎無過，乃奉鈔萬緡為壽，求交驩，文忠却之。

translations.literal: " That man bore ill will toward Wenzhong and wished to strike him down through a trap; yet because Wenzhong was pure, careful, and without fault, he instead offered ten thousand strings of paper money as a birthday gift, seeking cordial friendship — Wenzhong refused it.
translations.idiomatic: " The man resented Wenzhong and hoped to destroy him, but finding Wenzhong irreproachably upright and cautious, he instead offered ten thousand strings of paper money as a birthday gift, seeking reconciliation. Wenzhong refused it.

sentences.zh: 文炳為中書左丞卒，太傅伯顏乃表文忠可相，帝使繼其官，文忠辭曰：「臣兄有平定南方之勞，可居是位。

translations.literal: Wenbing died while serving as left vice director of the Secretariat; Grand Preceptor Bayan then memorialized that Wenzhong was fit for chancellor. The emperor had him succeed to the office. Wenzhong declined, saying: "My elder brother had the merit of pacifying the south — he was fit to hold this position.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenbing died in office as left vice director of the Secretariat, Grand Preceptor Bayan memorialized that Wenzhong was fit to be chancellor. The emperor ordered Wenzhong to succeed him. Wenzhong declined, saying, "My elder brother earned the merit of pacifying the south — he deserved this post.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗給事居中，所宣何力，敢冒居重職乎！」

translations.literal: I merely served in attendance at the center — what force did I exert in proclaiming edicts that I should dare assume so weighty a post!"
translations.idiomatic: I merely served in attendance at court — what real contribution did I make in proclaiming edicts that I should dare take so weighty an office!"

sentences.zh: 十八年，陞典瑞局為監、郎為卿，仍以文忠為之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Directorate of Auspicious Insignia was promoted from bureau to directorate, and its clerks to ministers; Wenzhong continued to hold the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the Directorate of Auspicious Insignia was elevated from bureau to directorate and its officers promoted to ministerial rank; Wenzhong retained the directorship.

sentences.zh: 授正議大夫，俄授資德大夫、僉書樞密院事，卿如故。

translations.literal: He was granted Righteous Consultant Grand Master; shortly afterward he was granted Grand Master of Brilliant Talent and made associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, while retaining the directorate post.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Righteous Consultant Grand Master; soon afterward he was promoted to Grand Master of Brilliant Talent and appointed associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, while keeping his directorate post.

sentences.zh: 車駕行幸，詔文忠毋扈從，留居大都，凡宮苑、城門、直舍、徼道、環衛、營屯、禁兵、太府、少府、軍器、尚乘諸監，皆領焉。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage traveled on tour, an edict ordered Wenzhong not to accompany it; he remained in residence at the Great Capital, overseeing the palace parks, city gates, straight lodgings, patrol routes, guard encirclements, camp garrisons, forbidden troops, the Imperial Storehouse, Lesser Storehouse, Armaments, and Imperial Mount directorates — all fell under his charge.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled, an edict ordered Wenzhong to remain in the Great Capital rather than accompany the procession. He was put in charge of the palace grounds, city gates, guard posts, patrol routes, encampments, forbidden troops, and the Imperial Storehouse, Lesser Storehouse, Armaments, and Imperial Mount directorates.

sentences.zh: 兵馬司舊隸中書，併付文忠。

translations.literal: The Horse and Chariot Office, formerly subordinate to the Secretariat, was also entrusted to Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Horse and Chariot Office, formerly under the Secretariat, was also placed under Wenzhong's authority.

sentences.zh: 時權臣累請奪還中書，不報。

translations.literal: At that time the powerful minister repeatedly requested that [the office] be seized back for the Secretariat — no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: Around that time a powerful minister repeatedly pressed to strip the Secretariat of its authority and restore it to the central government, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 是冬十月二十有五日，雞鳴，將入朝，忽病仆，帝遣中使持藥投救不及，遂卒，甚悼惜之，賻錢數十萬。

translations.literal: That winter, on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month, at cockcrow, as he was about to enter court, he suddenly fell ill and collapsed; the emperor sent a palace messenger bearing medicine, but rescue came too late, and he died. The emperor deeply mourned and regretted it, granting burial money of several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, on the twenty-fifth of the tenth month, at cockcrow, as he was setting out for court, he suddenly collapsed in illness. The emperor dispatched a palace messenger with medicine, but help arrived too late and he died. The emperor grieved deeply and granted several hundred thousand in funeral funds.

sentences.zh: 後制贈光祿大夫、司徒，封壽國公，諡忠貞。

translations.literal: Later by decree he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Minister of Education, enfeoffed as Duke of Shou, with the posthumous title Zhongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequently an edict posthumously made him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Minister of Education, enfeoffed him as Duke of Shou, and gave him the posthumous name Zhongzhen (Loyal and True).

sentences.zh: 嚴實子忠濟 忠嗣

translations.literal: Yan Shi's sons Zhongji and Zhongsi
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi — his sons Zhongji and Zhongsi

sentences.zh: 嚴實字武叔，泰安長清人。

translations.literal: Yan Shi, styled Wushu, was a native of Changqing in Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi, courtesy name Wushu, came from Changqing in Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 略知書，志氣豪放，不治生產，喜交結施與，落魄里社間。

translations.literal: He had some knowledge of letters; his spirit was bold and uninhibited. He did not manage production, loved making connections and giving gifts, and lived at loose ends among the village communities.
translations.idiomatic: He had a modest education and a bold, expansive temperament. He neglected his livelihood, loved making friends and dispensing favors, and drifted freely among the villages.

sentences.zh: 屢以事繫獄，俠少輩為出死力，乃得脫去。

translations.literal: Repeatedly imprisoned for various matters; young men of the gallant sort expended all their strength for him, and only thus did he escape.
translations.idiomatic: He was jailed again and again for one affair or another, but young men of the gallant sort risked their lives on his behalf, and only then did he get free.

sentences.zh: 癸酉秋，太祖率兵自紫荊口入，分略山東、河北、河東而歸。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the guiyou year, Genghis Khan led troops in from Zijing Pass, divided forces to overrun Shandong, Hebei, and Hedong, then returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of guiyou, Genghis Khan led his army in through Zijing Pass, sent columns to overrun Shandong, Hebei, and Hedong, and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 金東平行臺調民為兵，以實為衆所服，命為百戶。

translations.literal: The Jin Eastern Branch Secretariat conscripted the people as soldiers; as Yan Shi was admired by the multitude, he was appointed a centurion.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Eastern Branch Secretariat conscripted the populace for military service. Because Yan Shi commanded the people's respect, he was made a centurion.

sentences.zh: 甲戌春，泰安張汝楫據靈巖，遣別將攻長清，實破走之。

translations.literal: In spring of the jiaxu year, Zhang Ruji of Tai'an held Lingyan, sent a deputy general to attack Changqing; Yan Shi defeated and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of jiaxu, Zhang Ruji of Tai'an seized Lingyan and sent a deputy general against Changqing; Yan Shi routed the force and drove it off.

sentences.zh: 以功授長清尉。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the post of Changqing commandant.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was appointed commandant of Changqing.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，權長清令。

translations.literal: In wuyin, he acted as magistrate of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: In wuyin he served as acting magistrate of Changqing.

sentences.zh: 宋取益都，乘勝而西，行臺檄實備芻糧為守禦計。

translations.literal: The Song took Yidu and, riding the momentum, marched west; the Branch Secretariat ordered Yan Shi to prepare fodder and grain for defensive plans.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song captured Yidu and pressed westward on the momentum of victory, the Branch Secretariat ordered Yan Shi to gather fodder and grain for the defense.

sentences.zh: 實出督租，比還，而長清破，俄以兵復之。

translations.literal: Yan Shi went out to supervise tax collection; when he returned, Changqing had fallen, but soon he recovered it by force of arms.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi went out to oversee tax collection, and by the time he returned Changqing had fallen; before long he retook it by force.

sentences.zh: 有譖于行臺者，謂實與宋有謀，行臺以兵圍之，實挈家避青崖。

translations.literal: Someone slandered him to the Branch Secretariat, saying Yan Shi had designs with the Song; the Branch Secretariat surrounded him with troops; Yan Shi took his family and fled to Qingya.
translations.idiomatic: Someone denounced him to the Branch Secretariat, claiming he was plotting with the Song. The Branch Secretariat sent troops to surround him, and Yan Shi fled with his family to Qingya.

sentences.zh: 宋因以實為濟南治中，分兵四出，所至無不下，於是太行之東，皆受實節制。

translations.literal: The Song thereupon made Yan Shi Administrative Assistant of Jinan; he sent troops out in four directions — wherever they went, none failed to fall; thus east of the Taihang Mountains all came under Yan Shi's command.
translations.idiomatic: The Song then appointed Yan Shi administrative assistant of Jinan. He sent troops out in every direction, and wherever they went the cities fell. East of the Taihang Mountains, all came under his command.

sentences.zh: 庚辰三月，金河南軍攻彰德，守將單仲力不支，數求救。

translations.literal: In the third month of gengchen, the Jin Henan army attacked Zhangde; the defending general Shan Zhong could not hold, and repeatedly sought rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of gengchen the Jin Henan army besieged Zhangde. The defending general Shan Zhong could not hold out and sent repeated pleas for help.

sentences.zh: 實請於主將張林，林逗遛不行，實獨以兵赴之，比至，而仲被擒。

translations.literal: Yan Shi requested of the commander-in-chief Zhang Lin; Lin stalled and would not go; Yan Shi alone led troops to the relief; when he arrived, Zhong had already been captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi appealed to the commander-in-chief Zhang Lin, but Lin dragged his feet and would not march. Yan Shi went alone with his troops, but by the time he arrived Shan Zhong had already been taken.

sentences.zh: 實知宋不足恃。

translations.literal: Yan Shi knew the Song could not be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi saw that the Song were not to be counted on.

sentences.zh: 七月，謁太師木華黎於軍門，挈所部彰德、大名、磁、洺、恩、博、滑、濬等州戶三十萬來歸，木華黎承制拜實金紫光祿大夫、行尚書省事。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he paid homage to Grand Preceptor Muqali at the army gate, bringing with him the households under his command from Zhangde, Daming, Ci, Ming, En, Bo, Hua, and Jun and other prefectures — three hundred thousand in all — to submit; Muqali, acting under imperial authority, appointed Yan Shi Golden-girdled Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Director of Secretariat Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he presented himself to Grand Preceptor Muqali at headquarters, bringing three hundred thousand households from Zhangde, Daming, Ci, Ming, En, Bo, Hua, Jun, and other prefectures under his command to submit. Muqali, acting by imperial commission, appointed Yan Shi Golden-girdled Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting director of Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 進攻曹、濮、單三州，皆下之。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack the three prefectures of Cao, Pu, and Shan — all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against the three prefectures of Cao, Pu, and Shan and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 偏將李信，留鎮青崖，嘗有罪，懼誅，乘實之出，殺其家屬，降于宋。

translations.literal: The deputy general Li Xin, left to garrison Qingya, had once committed a crime and feared execution; when Yan Shi went out, he killed Yan Shi's family members and surrendered to the Song.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy general Li Xin, left to hold Qingya, had earlier committed an offense and feared punishment. While Yan Shi was away he slaughtered Yan Shi's family and surrendered to the Song.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，實以兵復青崖，擒信誅之。

translations.literal: In xinsi, Yan Shi with troops recovered Qingya, captured Xin, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: In xinsi Yan Shi retook Qingya by force, captured Li Xin, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 進攻東平，金守將和立剛棄城遁，實入居之。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Dongping, the Jin defending general He Ligang abandoned the city and fled; Yan Shi entered and took up residence there.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Dongping; the Jin defender He Ligang abandoned the city and fled, and Yan Shi entered and made it his seat.

sentences.zh: 壬午，宋將彭義斌率師取京東州縣，實將晁海以青崖降，盡掠實家，義斌軍西下，郡縣多歸之。

translations.literal: In renowu, Song general Peng Yibin led troops to seize the prefectures and counties of eastern Jing; Yan Shi's general Chao Hai surrendered Qingya, plundered Yan Shi's household entirely; Peng Yibin's army marched west, and many commanderies and counties submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: In renowu the Song general Peng Yibin led an army to take the prefectures and counties of eastern Jing. Yan Shi's officer Chao Hai surrendered Qingya and looted Yan Shi's household clean. As Peng Yibin's army pushed west, commanderies and counties fell to him in large numbers.

sentences.zh: 乙酉四月，遂圍東平。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of yiyou, he then besieged Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of yiyou he laid siege to Dongping.

sentences.zh: 實潛約大將孛里海合兵攻之，兵久不至，城中食且盡，乃與義斌連和。

translations.literal: Yan Shi secretly arranged with Grand General Bolihai to combine forces and attack him; the troops long did not arrive; food in the city was nearly exhausted — he then made peace with Peng Yibin.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi secretly arranged with Grand General Bolihai to join forces and strike back, but the relief army was slow in coming and provisions in the city were nearly gone. He then made terms with Peng Yibin.

sentences.zh: 義斌亦欲藉實取河朔，而後圖之，請以兄事實。

translations.literal: Peng Yibin also wished to use Yan Shi to take Heshuo, and afterward plot against him — he requested to treat Yan Shi as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yibin also meant to use Yan Shi to seize Heshuo and deal with him later; he asked to treat Yan Shi as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 時麾下衆尚數千，義斌聽其自領，而青崖所掠者則留不遣。

translations.literal: At that time the forces under his command still numbered several thousand; Peng Yibin let him command them himself, but those plundered at Qingya he kept and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi still had several thousand men under his command, and Peng Yibin let him keep them, but the goods looted at Qingya he retained and would not release.

sentences.zh: 七月，義斌下真定，道西山，與孛里海等軍相望，分實以帳下兵，陽助而陰伺之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Peng Yibin took Zhending, by way of the western hills, and faced Bolihai's army and others across the distance; he assigned Yan Shi some of his personal troops — outwardly to assist, inwardly to watch him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Peng Yibin took Zhending by the western hills and came within sight of Bolihai's army and others. He detached some of his personal troops to Yan Shi — ostensibly to help, but in fact to keep watch on him.

sentences.zh: 實知勢迫，急赴孛里海軍與之合，遂與義斌戰，宋兵潰，擒義斌。

translations.literal: Yan Shi knew the situation was pressing; he hurried to Bolihai's army and joined with him; then they fought Peng Yibin — Song troops collapsed; Peng Yibin was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the pressure closing in, Yan Shi rushed to Bolihai's camp and joined him. They gave battle to Peng Yibin; the Song army broke, and Peng Yibin was taken.

sentences.zh: 不旬月，京東州縣復為實有。

translations.literal: Within less than ten days, the prefectures and counties of eastern Jing were again Yan Shi's.
translations.idiomatic: In less than ten days the prefectures and counties of eastern Jing were Yan Shi's once more.

sentences.zh: 是冬，木華黎之弟帶孫取彰德；

translations.literal: That winter, Muqali's younger brother Daisun took Zhangde;
translations.idiomatic: That winter Muqali's younger brother Daisun captured Zhangde;

sentences.zh: 明年，取濮、東平；

translations.literal: The next year, took Pu and Dongping;
translations.idiomatic: The following year he took Pu and Dongping;

sentences.zh: 又明年，木華黎之子孛魯取益都：實皆有功焉。

translations.literal: The year after that, Muqali's son Bolu took Yidu — Yan Shi had merit in all of these.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that Muqali's son Bolu captured Yidu — Yan Shi had a hand in each of these victories.

sentences.zh: 庚寅四月，朝太宗于牛心之幄殿，帝賜之坐，宴享終日，賜以虎符。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of gengyin he had audience with Ögedei at the Ox-Heart imperial tent hall; the emperor granted him a seat, feasted and entertained him the whole day, and bestowed a tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of gengyin he had audience with Ögedei in the Ox-Heart imperial tent hall. The emperor gave him a seat, feasted him through the day, and bestowed a tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 數顧實謂侍臣曰：「嚴實，真福人也。

translations.literal: Repeatedly turning to Yan Shi he said to attendant ministers: "Yan Shi — truly a man of fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Turning again and again toward Yan Shi, he said to his attendants, "Yan Shi is truly a man blessed by fortune.

sentences.zh: 」甲午，朝于和林，授東平路行軍萬戶，偏裨賜金符者八人。

translations.literal: " On jiawu he had audience at Karakorum, was appointed military ten-thousand-household commander of the Dongping Circuit, and eight deputy commanders were granted golden tallies.
translations.idiomatic: " On jiawu he had audience at Karakorum and was appointed military ten-thousand-household commander of the Dongping Circuit; eight of his deputy commanders received golden tallies.

sentences.zh: 先是，實之所統，凡五十餘城，至是，惟德、兗、濟、單隸東平。

translations.literal: Previously the territory Yan Shi commanded totaled more than fifty cities; at this time only De, Yan, Ji, and Shan were placed under Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Before this Yan Shi had governed more than fifty cities; now only De, Yan, Ji, and Shan were placed under Dongping.

sentences.zh: 丁酉九月，詔實毋事征伐。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of dingyou an edict ordered Yan Shi not to undertake campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of dingyou an edict ordered Yan Shi to refrain from campaigning.

sentences.zh: 初，彰德既下，又破水柵，帶孫怒其反覆，驅老幼數萬欲屠之。

translations.literal: Initially, after Zhangde had fallen and the water palisade was broken, Daisun was angry at their repeated shifting of allegiance and drove out tens of thousands of old and young intending to slaughter them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Zhangde had fallen and the water palisade was broken, Daisun was enraged at the people's repeated switching of sides and drove out tens of thousands of old and young to slaughter them.

sentences.zh: 實曰：「此國家舊民，吾兵力不能及，為所脅從，果何罪耶！

translations.literal: Yan Shi said: "These are the state's old subjects — my military force could not reach them; they were coerced into following [the enemy] — what crime is there indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi said, "These are the state's own people. My troops could not reach them; they were forced to follow the enemy — what crime have they committed!

sentences.zh: 」帶孫從之。

translations.literal: " Daisun followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Daisun accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 繼破濮州，復欲屠之。

translations.literal: Afterward Pu prefecture was taken, and again they wished to slaughter the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu Prefecture was taken next, they again intended to massacre the population.

sentences.zh: 實言：「百姓未嘗敵我，豈可與執兵刃者同戮，不若留之，以供芻秣。

translations.literal: Yan Shi said: "The common people never opposed us — how can they be put to the same slaughter as those who bore weapons? Better to keep them to supply fodder and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi argued, "The common people never fought us — how can they be punished like armed soldiers? Better to keep them alive to supply fodder and grain.

sentences.zh: 」濮人免者又數萬。

translations.literal: " Tens of thousands among the people of Pu were spared again.
translations.idiomatic: " Tens of thousands of people in Pu were spared once more.

sentences.zh: 其後於曹、楚丘、定陶、上黨皆然。

translations.literal: Afterward at Cao, Chuqiu, Dingtao, Shangdang — all were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the same thing happened at Cao, Chuqiu, Dingtao, and Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 時兵由武關出襄、鄧，實在徐、邳間，以為河南破，屠戮必多，乃載金繒往贖之，且約束諸將，毋敢妄有殺掠。

translations.literal: At that time troops went out through Wuguan toward Xiang and Deng; Yan Shi was between Xu and Pi; he thought that when Henan fell slaughter would certainly be extensive — he therefore loaded gold and silks to go ransom people, and moreover restrained the generals: none dare recklessly kill and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the army marched out through Wuguan toward Xiang and Deng while Yan Shi was stationed between Xu and Pi. Fearing that when Henan fell the slaughter would be great, he loaded gold and silks to ransom captives and strictly ordered his generals not to kill or plunder at will.

sentences.zh: 靈壁一縣，當誅者五萬人，實悉救之。

translations.literal: In Lingbi county alone, fifty thousand were marked for execution — Yan Shi rescued them all.
translations.idiomatic: In Lingbi county alone fifty thousand were marked for death; Yan Shi saved them all.

sentences.zh: 會大饑，民北徙者多餓死。

translations.literal: There came a great famine; many of the people migrating north died of starvation.
translations.idiomatic: A great famine struck, and many of the people fleeing north starved to death.

sentences.zh: 又法，藏匿逃者，保社皆坐。

translations.literal: Moreover by law, whoever concealed fugitives — the mutual-responsibility groups all were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: The law also held that anyone who hid fugitives made his entire mutual-responsibility group liable.

sentences.zh: 逃亡無所託，殭尸蔽野，實命作糜粥，盛置道傍，全活者衆。

translations.literal: Fugitives had nowhere to take refuge; corpses lay stiff and covered the fields; Yan Shi ordered gruel made and placed abundantly beside the roads — many were fully saved.
translations.idiomatic: With nowhere to turn, fugitives died until the fields were covered with corpses. Yan Shi ordered gruel prepared and set out in abundance along the roads, and many lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 實部曲有逃歸益都者數十人，益都破，皆獲之，以為必殺，實置不問。

translations.literal: Several tens of Yan Shi's retainers had fled back to Yidu; when Yidu fell they were all captured — it was thought they would certainly be killed — Yan Shi set the matter aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen of Yan Shi's retainers had fled back to Yidu; when Yidu fell they were all captured and everyone assumed they would be executed, but Yan Shi let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 王義深者，義斌之別將，聞義斌敗，將奔河南，實族屬在東平者，皆為所害。

translations.literal: Wang Yishen was Peng Yibin's deputy general; hearing Peng Yibin had been defeated, he was about to flee to Henan — Yan Shi's kinsmen in Dongping were all harmed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yishen was a deputy general under Peng Yibin. When he heard of Peng Yibin's defeat and prepared to flee to Henan, he killed every member of Yan Shi's clan he could find in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 河南破，實獲義深妻子，厚周卹之，送還鄉里，終不以舊怨為嫌。

translations.literal: When Henan fell Yan Shi captured Yishen's wife and children, generously supported and comforted them, and sent them back to their home district — in the end he did not treat old grudges as cause for resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan fell Yan Shi captured Yishen's wife and children, treated them generously, and sent them home — never letting old grievances stand in the way.

sentences.zh: 其寬厚長者類若此。

translations.literal: His generous and elder-like conduct was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His magnanimity and elder-like kindness were of this kind throughout.

sentences.zh: 庚子卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: In gengzi he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in gengzi at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 遠近悲悼，野哭巷祭，旬月不已。

translations.literal: Near and far grieved and mourned; weeping in the fields and sacrifices in the lanes continued for a month without cease.
translations.idiomatic: People near and far mourned him; wailing filled the countryside and offerings lined the lanes, and this continued for a month without end.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，追封實為魯國公，諡武惠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong, Yan Shi was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lu, with the posthumous title Wuhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lu with the posthumous name Wuhui (Martial and Beneficent).

sentences.zh: 子忠貞，金紫光祿大夫；

translations.literal: His son Zhongzhen, Golden-girdled Grand Master of Splendid Happiness;
translations.idiomatic: His sons included Zhongzhen, Golden-girdled Grand Master of Splendid Happiness;

sentences.zh: 忠濟，忠嗣，忠範，忠傑，忠裕，忠祐。

translations.literal: Zhongji, Zhongsi, Zhongfan, Zhongjie, Zhongyu, Zhongyou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongji, Zhongsi, Zhongfan, Zhongjie, Zhongyu, and Zhongyou.

sentences.zh: 忠濟，一名忠翰，字紫芝，實之第二子也。

translations.literal: Zhongji, also called Zhonghan, styled Zizhi, was Yan Shi's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongji — also known as Zhonghan, courtesy name Zizhi — was Yan Shi's second son.

sentences.zh: 儀觀雄偉，善騎射。

translations.literal: His bearing was imposing and stately; he was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He had a commanding presence and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，從其父入見太宗，命佩虎符，襲東平路行軍萬戶、管民長官，開府布政，一法其父。

translations.literal: In xinchou he accompanied his father to audience with Ögedei; he was ordered to wear the tiger tally, succeeding to military ten-thousand-household commander of Dongping Circuit and civilian administrator; he opened a headquarters and governed — all modeled on his father.
translations.idiomatic: In xinchou he accompanied his father to audience with Ögedei and was ordered to wear the tiger tally, succeeding as military ten-thousand-household commander of the Dongping Circuit and civilian administrator. He opened a headquarters and governed after his father's model in every respect.

sentences.zh: 養老尊賢，治為諸道第一。

translations.literal: He nurtured the aged and honored the worthy; his governance ranked first among all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for the elderly and honored the worthy, and his administration ranked first among all circuits.

sentences.zh: 領兵略地淮、漢，偏裨部曲，戮力用命。

translations.literal: Leading troops to seize territory in Huai and Han, deputy commanders and retainers exerted their strength and obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: Leading troops to expand territory along the Huai and Han, his deputies and retainers gave their full strength and obeyed without fail.

sentences.zh: 定宗、憲宗即位之始，皆加褒寵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the enthronements of Güyük and Möngke, added honors and favor were both granted.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of both Güyük's and Möngke's reigns he received added honors and favor.

sentences.zh: 忠濟初統千戶十有七，乙卯，朝命括新軍山東，益兵二萬有奇。

translations.literal: Zhongji initially commanded seventeen centurions; in yimao the court ordered a levy of new troops in Shandong, increasing his force by more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongji initially commanded seventeen centurions. In yimao the court ordered a recruitment of new troops in Shandong, adding more than twenty thousand to his army.

sentences.zh: 忠濟弟忠嗣、忠範為萬戶，以次諸弟暨勳將之子為千戶，城戍宿州、蘄縣，而忠濟皆統之。

translations.literal: Zhongji's younger brothers Zhongsi and Zhongfan were made ten-thousand-household commanders; his other younger brothers in order and the sons of meritorious generals were made centurions; they garrisoned Suzhou and Qixian, and Zhongji commanded them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongji's younger brothers Zhongsi and Zhongfan were made ten-thousand-household commanders; his other brothers in turn and the sons of meritorious generals were made centurions. They garrisoned Suzhou and Qixian, all under Zhongji's overall command.

sentences.zh: 己未，世祖南伐，詔率師由間道會鄂。

translations.literal: In jiwei Kublai campaigned south; an edict ordered him to lead troops by a hidden route to rendezvous at E.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei, when Kublai launched his southern campaign, an edict ordered Zhongji to lead his army by a concealed route to join the forces at Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 親率勇士，梯衝登城。

translations.literal: He personally led brave warriors, scaling the walls with siege ladders and rams.
translations.idiomatic: He personally led his bravest men up the walls on scaling ladders and battering rams.

sentences.zh: 師還，忠濟選勇敢二千，別命千戶將之，甲仗精銳，所向無前。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Zhongji selected two thousand brave men, separately appointing centurions to command them; their armor and weapons were keen and sharp — wherever they went none stood before them.
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew, Zhongji picked out two thousand of his bravest men and put centurions in command of them. Their arms and armor were first-rate, and they swept all before them.

sentences.zh: 大臣有言其威權太盛者。

translations.literal: Some ministers said his authority and power were too great.
translations.idiomatic: Some ministers complained that his power had grown too great.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，召還京師，命忠範代之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong he was recalled to the capital; Zhongfan was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong he was recalled to the capital and Zhongfan was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 忠濟治東平日，借貸於人，代部民納逋賦，歲久愈多。

translations.literal: While Zhongji governed Dongping he borrowed from others to pay overdue taxes on behalf of the people under his command; as the years passed the debt grew ever larger.
translations.idiomatic: During his years governing Dongping, Zhongji borrowed money to pay overdue taxes for the people under his command, and the debt mounted year after year.

sentences.zh: 及謝事，債家執文券來徵。

translations.literal: When he left office, creditors came with written bonds to collect payment.
translations.idiomatic: When he stepped down, creditors arrived with written bonds to collect what they were owed.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，悉命發內藏代償。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he ordered the entire sum paid from the inner treasury on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, he ordered the full amount paid from the imperial treasury on Zhongji's behalf.

sentences.zh: 東平廟學故隘陋，改卜高爽地于城東，教養諸生，後多顯者。

translations.literal: The temple school of Dongping was formerly narrow and shabby; he chose a high, open site east of the city and moved it there, educating and nurturing students — many later became eminent.
translations.idiomatic: The Dongping temple school had been cramped and dilapidated; he relocated it to open high ground east of the city and nurtured its students, many of whom later rose to distinction.

sentences.zh: 幕僚如宋子貞、劉肅、李昶、徐世隆，俱為名臣。

translations.literal: Staff members such as Song Zizhen, Liu Su, Li Chang, and Xu Shilong all became renowned ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Among his staff were Song Zizhen, Liu Su, Li Chang, and Xu Shilong — all of whom became celebrated ministers.

sentences.zh: 至元二十三年，特授資德大夫、中書左丞、行江浙省事，以老辭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Zhiyuan he was specially granted Grand Master of Brilliant Talent, left vice director of the Secretariat, and acting director of Jiang-Zhe affairs; he declined on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Zhiyuan he was specially appointed Grand Master of Brilliant Talent, left vice director of the Secretariat, and acting director of Jiang-Zhe affairs, but declined on grounds of age.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，賜鈔萬五千緡、宅一區，召其子瑜入侍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was granted ten thousand five hundred strings of paper money and one residence; his son Yu was summoned to attend at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he received ten thousand five hundred strings of paper money and a residence, and his son Yu was summoned to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 三十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirtieth year.

sentences.zh: 忠濟統理方郡凡十一年，爵人命官，生殺予奪，皆自己出。

translations.literal: Zhongji governed the regional prefecture for eleven years in all; ennoblements, appointments, life and death, granting and taking — all issued from himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongji governed his region for eleven years in all, wielding sole authority over ennoblements, appointments, and the power of life and death.

sentences.zh: 及謝去大權，貴而能貧，安于義命，世以是多之。

translations.literal: When he relinquished great power, though noble he could be poor, content with fate and duty — the world therefore praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: When he gave up his great authority he lived in honorable poverty, content with his lot, and the world admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 後諡莊孝。

translations.literal: Later he was given the posthumous title Zhuangxiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was later given the posthumous name Zhuangxiao (Dignified and Filial).

sentences.zh: 忠嗣，實之第三子也。

translations.literal: Zhongsi was Yan Shi's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi was Yan Shi's third son.

sentences.zh: 少從張澄、商挺、李楨學，略知經史大義。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Zhang Cheng, Shang Ting, and Li Zhen, and gained some knowledge of the essential meaning of the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied under Zhang Cheng, Shang Ting, and Li Zhen and gained a working knowledge of the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，其兄忠濟授以東平人匠緫管，遙領單州防禦使事。

translations.literal: In xinhai his elder brother Zhongji appointed him overall supervisor of Dongping artisans, and he remotely held the duties of defensive commissioner of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In xinhai his elder brother Zhongji made him overall supervisor of Dongping artisans and gave him nominal charge of the defensive commissioner post at Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，充東平路管軍萬戶。

translations.literal: In yimao he served as military ten-thousand-household commander of the Dongping Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In yimao he was appointed military ten-thousand-household commander of the Dongping Circuit.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，從忠濟略地揚州，取邵伯埭，首立戰功。

translations.literal: In dingsi he followed Zhongji to seize territory in Yangzhou, took Shaobo Dam, and was first to establish merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In dingsi he followed Zhongji in the campaign around Yangzhou, captured Shaobo Dam, and won the first battle honors.

sentences.zh: 己未南征，從忠濟渡淮，分兵出挂車嶺，與宋兵相拒三晝夜，殺獲甚衆，始達蘄州。

translations.literal: In the southern campaign of jiwei he followed Zhongji across the Huai, sent troops out through Guache Ridge, and held off Song troops for three days and nights, killing and capturing many before reaching Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign of jiwei he crossed the Huai with Zhongji, sent a detachment through Guache Ridge, and fought the Song army for three days and nights, killing and capturing many before reaching Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 及渡江抵鄂，分部攻城九十餘日，戰甚力。

translations.literal: When they crossed the Yangtze and reached E, he divided forces to besiege the city for more than ninety days, fighting with great vigor.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Yangtze and reaching Ezhou, he took part in the siege for more than ninety days and fought with great tenacity.

sentences.zh: 師還，授金虎符。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was granted a golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew he was awarded a golden tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，李璮叛，宋兵攻蘄縣，勢張甚，徐州緫管李杲哥降于宋，齊魯山寨為宋兵所據。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong Li Tan rebelled; Song troops attacked Qixian with greatly swelling momentum; Xuzhou overall supervisor Li Gaoge surrendered to the Song; the stockades of Qi and Lu were seized by Song troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhongtong Li Tan rebelled. Song troops attacked Qixian with great force; Xuzhou overall supervisor Li Gaoge surrendered to the Song, and the mountain stockades of Qi and Lu fell to Song hands.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣從大帥按脫救蘄縣，復徐州，執李杲哥殺之。

translations.literal: Zhongsi followed the grand commander Antu to relieve Qixian, recovered Xuzhou, seized Li Gaoge, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi followed Grand Commander Antu to relieve Qixian, retook Xuzhou, captured Li Gaoge, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 攻鄒之嶧山、滕之牙山，多所殺獲。

translations.literal: Attacking Yishan in Zou and Yashan in Teng, he killed and captured many.
translations.idiomatic: In attacks on Yishan in Zou and Yashan in Teng he killed and captured large numbers of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 按脫論功以聞，賜銀二百兩、幣五十端。

translations.literal: Antu reported his merits according to merit; he was granted two hundred taels of silver and fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Antu submitted a report of his achievements, and he was rewarded with two hundred taels of silver and fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 四年，朝廷懲青齊之亂，居大藩者，子弟不得親政，於是罷官家居。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the court, punishing the disorder of Qing and Qi, ruled that those holding great regional fiefs could not have their sons and younger brothers hold direct power; he therefore was dismissed from office and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, in the aftermath of the Qing-Qi rebellion, the court barred the sons and brothers of great regional lords from holding direct power, and Zhongsi was dismissed to live at home.

sentences.zh: 至元十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhiyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Zhiyuan.
